[1] Combat capability and sustainability

[2] S (2015–2016) Bill to the Storting (proposal for a Storting resolution

[3] Introduction and summary – Combat power and sustainability A strengthened and renewed defense The defense of the country is one of the state's most important tasks, and the ability to handle crisis and armed conflict in our own and allies' immediate areas must be given higher priority

[4] Only the Armed Forces can solve these tasks

[5] There are no quick solutions to building up defense capabilities, but the government's recommendation in this long-term plan ensures that Norway has a defense with robust and flexible operational departments that can handle changing challenges at home and abroad in light of the current threat landscape

[6] Norway has a defense that delivers high quality at home and abroad

[7] Norway's security is built together with others

[8] Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, stating that an armed attack against one or more Allies shall be considered an attack against them all, has been a pillar of Norwegian security policy for almost 70 years

[9] At the same time, the same treaty contains an important and significant responsibility in Article 3, which obliges NATO member states to maintain and develop their individual and collective ability to resist armed attack

[10] NATO cooperation requires a credible national defense that can react quickly and carry out coordinated operations, while receiving allied support, building up its own forces, and protecting the population and infrastructure

[11] The Armed Forces' level of ambition and requirements for preparedness must be changed in light of a new security policy situation, future international operations and the Armed Forces' significant contribution to society's overall preparedness

[12] It is particularly important to strengthen preparedness and the ability to handle the most extensive tasks

[13] defense against threats, attacks and attacks

[14] In order for defense capabilities to be maintained over time, and as a basis for economic sustainability, realistic planning that takes into account actual operating expenses and real cost developments is crucial

[15] The costs of operating and further developing a modern and relevant defense have been increasing over time

[16] This long-term plan takes such a development into account in the cost calculations for the first time

[17] The structure and capabilities of the armed forces must be constantly modernized to remain relevant in relation to potential adversaries and to be able to operate together with allies

[18] The current defense structure cannot be continued with the current budget level

[19] Previously, modernization costs have been covered through streamlining operations

[20] The number of units within several capacities has also been cut to such an extent that a number of capacities are currently at what must be considered the critical minimum to be able to deliver operational value and impact

[21] Another tool that has been used to finance previous restructuring is to accept a reduced level of operational activity for a period of time

[22] Today's security policy developments place increased demands on the Armed Forces' operational activities, making such prioritization unacceptable

[23] To further develop the Armed Forces and strengthen its real operational capability, the government is proposing a double boost for sustainability, with a combination of a historic strengthening of the defense budget and a number of structural measures

[24] This will lay the foundation for a long-term and sustainable development of the defense structure with a real balance between tasks, structure and finances

[25] Continuous modernization and reform is a requirement in all parts of the public sector

[26] This also applies to the defense sector

[27] There is a need for modernization and efficiency improvements to ensure that the Armed Forces' capabilities are relevant and provide the greatest possible impact

[28] Comprehensive structural and basic measures and continued efficiency improvements will ensure adaptation to changes in operational requirements, but also that resources are prioritized towards the most important areas

[29] The government's long-term plan assumes significant reallocation of resources within the defense sector to prioritized activities

[30] Increased allocations and the release of resources internally will firstly ensure that the identified backlog that has built up over time is caught up, so that availability and sustainability are increased

[31] Furthermore, increased resources will ensure that the Armed Forces' capabilities are practiced, trained and staffed so that they can be used for the tasks for which they are intended when needed

[32] Thirdly, the government proposes to invest in future-oriented, strategic capacities, among other things, to maintain situational awareness and control in the High North

[33] Solving the problems that have built up over time and laying the foundation for the sector to maintain sustainability in the future will take time and require a willingness to set clear priorities, tough measures and the ability to implement them

[34] The next two four-year periods will be challenging for the defense sector, even with the economic planning framework proposed by the government

[35] Significant savings related to the rationalization measures recommended by the government cannot be planned early in the period, since for many of the measures, restructuring costs will first be incurred or it will be necessary to carry out investments before the measures have an effect

[36] At the same time, the costs associated with several large investments in crucial capacities are incurred during the same period

[37] An important exception is the education area, where the financial benefits of the changes come early and, together with the increase in funding, are one of the prerequisites for financial sustainability early in the four-year period

[38] A sustainable and balanced structure requires significant and predictable increases in funding for the defense sector

[39] In the next two four-year periods, the government is emphasizing an economic planning framework that facilitates a gradual increase in the level of ambition for the defense sector

[40] In the further development of the Armed Forces' operational structure for the period 2017–2020, availability, endurance and better maintenance of current readiness times shall be prioritized

[41] From 2018, the government wants to increase the current level of ambition to include shorter readiness times, increased activity and increased staffing of selected capacities

[42] At the same time, extensive modernization will be continued and further strengthened from 2019 with the acquisition of materiel systems in the period 2021–2024, which will further strengthen operational capability, so that the Armed Forces remain a relevant security policy instrument for Norway

[43] The basis for the long-term plan In working on the new long-term plan, the government has emphasized openness, realism and sustainable solutions

[44] Openness about the challenges facing the Armed Forces, realism about capabilities and their actual operational status, and prioritization of sustainable solutions that stand the test of time and can be operated over time

[45] The defense sector's long-term plans shall ensure long-term and sustainable development of the sector based on updated assessments of relevant conditions

[46] To ensure a good basis for the government's choices and priorities, the government has obtained several important inputs for its work

[47] The most central of these is the Chief of Defence's professional military council

[48] The Chief of Defence was asked by the government to prioritize the ability to solve the most important and demanding tasks, including strengthening preparedness and the ability to build up forces

[49] Furthermore, the Expert Group for the Defense of Norway has delivered the report "A Common Lift", with a number of recommendations for strengthening defense capabilities

[50] The National Security Authority (NSM) presented its security advice with an overview of the challenges and possible risk-reducing measures within preventive security

[51] The government-appointed Conscription Committee presented its report "A Future Conscription System" on the further development of conscription and initial service

[52] The Ministry of Defence has also obtained an external consultant report on efficiency improvement with an assessment of the potential gains associated with staff, support and management functions in the sector

[53] In order to assess the consequences for society, a district-wide impact assessment has been carried out in dialogue with the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation

[54] A socio-economic analysis has also been conducted for the location of a forward base for combat aircraft and a base for maritime surveillance resources in Northern Norway

[55] In addition to the Ministry of Defence's own basic analyses, the Norwegian Defence Research Institute has provided key input

[56] The long-term planning work has also drawn on external studies, such as NOU

[57] Digital vulnerability – secure society (Lysne Committee

[58] The government has wanted to facilitate an open and broad debate about the further development of the defense sector

[59] In this connection, a separate portal was created, where private individuals, associations, municipalities, county authorities and other stakeholders were given the opportunity to provide their input into the long-term planning work

[60] Furthermore, the Minister of Defense invited dialogue meetings with affected municipalities and county authorities

[61] The personnel organizations have also been given the opportunity to provide their input into the basis

[62] Continuous long-term planning The Storting agreed in Recommendation

[63] S. no. 318, cf. St.prop

[64] No. 48 (2007–

[65] – A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values, towards a more continuous planning model for the defense sector

[66] The Storting will continue to be presented with and consider an overall, holistic perspective on the development of the defense sector in each parliamentary term

[67] At the same time, long-term planning will not be centered around fixed, four-year planning periods to the same extent as before

[68] The challenge of developing and renewing the defense sector has implications that extend over several parliamentary terms

[69] This long-term plan describes and guides development in the next four-year period (2017–

[70] But the plan also contains guidelines for development and operational and financial consequences in a longer perspective

[71] In the continuous planning model, greater emphasis is also placed on ongoing development of the sector and on matters being presented to the Storting when there is a need to inform or invite the Storting to make decisions on a matter

[72] Therefore, this long-term plan also outlines topics that the government will continue to work on and present to the Storting during the four-year period

[73] The continuous planning model proposes that the development of the defense sector should be a more continuous effort and that the long-term plans will not be comprehensive reassessments of the structure of the Armed Forces to the same extent as before

[74] Nevertheless, the challenges and developments facing the defense sector this time have necessitated a more comprehensive process and thorough and holistic priorities related to the sector's future development

[75] The transformation of the Armed Forces into a combat-ready force in the decades after the Cold War was necessary and appropriate given the challenges Norway faced

[76] Assumptions that have formed the basis of Norwegian defense planning since the end of the Cold War are changing

[77] Previous long-term plan (Prop

[78] Prop. 73 S (2011–

[79] A defense for our time was written in another time

[80] Since the current long-term plan was presented in 2012, Norway has witnessed greater security policy changes than in many years

[81] Security policy developments are bringing to light already existing challenges related to the Armed Forces' responsiveness, availability and endurance

[82] Decades of low tension at home, while the Armed Forces have had large and demanding tasks abroad, have meant that sufficient resources have not been prioritized for preparedness, maintenance and logistics for operations in the upper conflict spectrum

[83] The Armed Forces do not have the necessary ability to solve the most important tasks or the responsiveness and endurance that correspond to what the threat landscape requires

[84] The seriousness of the Armed Forces' reduced operational capability is reinforced by a strained economic situation and security policy and technological developments that result in increased demands on the Armed Forces

[85] This constitutes a demanding starting point for the new long-term plan

[86] The security policy, economic and technological changes are so extensive that, in the government's view, there is a need for a much greater investment in the Armed Forces in combination with clearer prioritization of the composition and organization of the Armed Forces

[87] With this long-term plan, the Government will strengthen the operational capability of the Armed Forces

[88] The Armed Forces must be able to carry out daily national tasks, contribute to credible deterrence and maintain Norway's role and expertise in strategic matters in the High North

[89] By increasing readiness stocks and carrying out necessary maintenance, the government will increase the responsiveness and endurance of our military forces

[90] The intelligence service is being further strengthened, and activity in the defense branches is being increased

[91] Furthermore, the government prioritizes investing in key, future-oriented capacities

[92] To achieve this, a combination of a significant economic boost, continued efficiency improvements, reprioritization of resources and structural changes is needed

[93] Development trends, frameworks and guidelines

[94] Norwegian security and defense policy aims to ensure Norway's sovereignty, territorial integrity and political freedom of action

[95] The basic rationale of the Armed Forces is to have a deterrent effect on potential attackers, and defend Norway and allies against external threats, attacks and threats

[96] Security and defense policy must enable Norway to respond to challenges across the entire crisis spectrum, from incident management in peacetime to a security crisis and armed conflict

[97] In this context, the armed forces are a fundamental and crucial security policy instrument

[98] Norwegian security and defense policy is based on a solid international framework, a strong transatlantic security community through NATO, and society's overall contribution to defense capabilities

[99] The foundation of Norway's security is NATO

[100] A modern defense that is part of a strong and credible alliance has a deterrent effect and reduces the likelihood that we will find ourselves in a situation where Norway's or our allies' security is challenged and must be defended with military force

[101] The Norwegian Armed Forces, together with allies, must be able to prevent hostile actors from gaining a strategic advantage by establishing themselves on Norwegian or allied territory or challenging our sovereignty

[102] The Armed Forces must have the ability to solve a broad range of national tasks and be able to contribute effectively to allied and other international cooperation for peace and security

[103] The Armed Forces should also be able to contribute substantially and effectively to strengthened security in cooperation with other key actors such as the UN, the EU, the Nordic countries and the African Union

[104] The Armed Forces play an important role in society's overall preparedness

[105] The Armed Forces shall contribute to societal security and national crisis management within the framework of total defense

[106] The Armed Forces shall cooperate with and support the police and civil emergency authorities in connection with terrorist attacks and other serious incidents, accidents and natural disasters

[107] Furthermore, the Armed Forces shall be developed within a comprehensive framework that ensures that the various elements complement and reinforce each other, and provide a balanced defense

[108] Operational capability, availability and preparedness must be strengthened

[109] The Armed Forces' overall operational capabilities must be trained, manned and equipped for joint operational efforts within the entire task portfolio

[110] The structure must be sustainable in both the short and long term

[111] Norwegian security and defense policy

[112] The changed security policy situation places greater demands on Norway to be able to take responsibility for its own security

[113] The Government's security policy priorities in this long-term plan are therefore to strengthen the defense of Norway, strengthen NATO's collective defense and contribute to international efforts

[114] In addition, the government will further develop total defense

[115] This includes both the Armed Forces' support for societal security and civil society's support for the Armed Forces in times of crisis and armed conflict

[116] Strengthening the defense of Norway requires that situational awareness in its own immediate areas is maintained and that the Armed Forces' operational capability is strengthened through improved responsiveness, combat power and endurance

[117] It is also important to increase military presence, exercises and training, and facilitate allied reinforcements

[118] The Government will link the Alliance and close allies more closely to Norway and Norwegian interests in daily life and throughout the entire spectrum of crises, and seek closer cooperation with selected allies

[119] This has a security policy dimension, but Norway should also seek multinational cooperation solutions as a cost-effective measure to maintain military capabilities

[120] Norwegian involvement in and contributions to NATO must be further strengthened, and arrangements must be made for NATO activity and presence in Norway

[121] Norway will contribute to international efforts and be a driving force in ensuring that NATO prioritizes collective defense

[122] The tasks of the Armed Forces are summarized as follows

[123] Ensure credible deterrence based on NATO's collective defense Defend Norway and allies against serious threats, attacks and attacks, within the framework of NATO's collective defense Prevent and handle incidents and security policy crises with national resources, including facilitating allied engagement Ensure a national basis for decision-making through surveillance and intelligence

[124] Asserted Norwegian sovereignty and sovereign rights

[125] Maintain the exercise of authority in defined areas Participate in multinational crisis management, including peace operations Contribute to international cooperation in the area of security and defense policy Contribute to the maintenance of public security and other central societal tasks

[126] Framework conditions and development since the previous long-term plan

[127] The security policy situation in our part of the world is, in sum, more demanding and complex than it has been for a long time

[128] Major challenges close to NATO's area of ​​responsibility can have direct consequences for Norwegian and allied security

[129] Russia's increased military capability and use of force constitute the most central change

[130] NATO's southern neighbourhood is characterized by conflict, large areas with weak government control, militant extremism and refugee flows

[131] These challenges come in addition to challenges in European countries and already existing security challenges related to global developments

[132] Reduced defense budgets in several NATO countries and pressure on collective defense capabilities are intensifying the challenges for Norway

[133] Norway has a shared responsibility for international peace and stability and must continue to be prepared to contribute to international military efforts at relatively short notice

[134] The technological developments that characterize society as a whole have a particularly significant impact on the Armed Forces

[135] This provides new opportunities to solve tasks more efficiently and with lower risk for personnel

[136] At the same time, the cost development for new technology poses a particular challenge for the Armed Forces

[137] The structure, competence profile and conceptual approach of the Armed Forces must be adapted to technological developments in order to obtain full benefit and combat power from the investments that have been made and are being made in high-tech equipment

[138] The need for continuous performance improvements means that the Armed Forces are experiencing high cost growth

[139] A backlog has built up over a long period of time in emergency logistics and maintenance, which must be addressed before efforts to increase activity and new investments have an effect

[140] The government is planning a historic increase in the defense budget in combination with further internal efficiency measures to free up resources for use by the Armed Forces

[141] Improvements and efficiency improvements are planned within the base structure, procurement and operation of buildings and facilities

[142] The savings should be sourced as much as possible within staff, support and administration and reprioritized to operational activities

[143] Extensive changes are being initiated within the Armed Forces' education system

[144] All savings will be used to strengthen the Armed Forces' ability to carry out its tasks

[145] The Armed Forces and Society

[146] The defense of the country is the defense sector's main mission

[147] But the defense sector is also a significant societal player in other areas

[148] The direct economic effect of the Armed Forces' presence and activity in the country is approximately NOK 30 billion

[149] The Armed Forces are in a mutually dependent relationship with other emergency response authorities

[150] The total defense concept involves mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society in connection with prevention, emergency planning, crisis and consequence management across the entire crisis spectrum, from peace via security policy crises to armed conflict

[151] The government is further developing the defense sector's ability to assist civilian authorities in public security

[152] The Armed Forces' own needs will still be most important for developing the Armed Forces' structure and capabilities

[153] The Armed Forces' support for civil society should nevertheless be a greater determinant of the organization and dimensioning of the Armed Forces' capacities

[154] This applies particularly in the areas of maritime counterterrorism and infectious disease transport

[155] In the case of major investments in the Armed Forces that may have beneficial value for civilian authorities, it must be clarified whether there is a need for assistance and support and opportunities for multiple use

[156] Such possible needs and opportunities must be included in the assessment

[157] Further development of the Armed Forces' structure

[158] The Government will ensure that the Armed Forces are robust and flexible, so that it can handle changing challenges

[159] The defence policy provides the basis for the adaptation of the structure of the Armed Forces and links the overall political ambitions and priorities for the Armed Forces with the specific design of the Armed Forces' structure, organisation and activities

[160] The government prioritizes the acquisition of strategic capabilities

[161] Capabilities such as submarines, maritime surveillance aircraft and F-35 fighter jets are important contributions to the Norwegian Armed Forces' deterrence capability and to NATO's collective defense capability

[162] Reductions in some selected areas provide the opportunity to invest in new, modern and effective systems, while also helping to strengthen important existing capacities and increase their availability and endurance

[163] Norway's ability to establish national and allied situational awareness in the North is prioritized through strengthening several capacities that contribute in such a context

[164] There is a need to investigate how technological and conceptual developments will have long-term consequences for future land forces

[165] The government is therefore implementing a comprehensive assessment of future land power

[166] At the same time, the Army will be strengthened from 2017 by improving the operational situation, increasing the level of activity and rectifying deficiencies in emergency logistics

[167] The base and support structure The Government will improve the balance between the operational structure and the performance of support activities

[168] The base and support structure has not been modernized in line with the major restructuring of the operational structure

[169] The goal is to ensure a long-term balance between the Armed Forces' operational structure, force production, bases and support activities, so that a larger part of the sector's resources can be used for operational activities and their support

[170] The Government will therefore make a much-needed reduction in the number of bases, streamline management and continue the modernization of logistics

[171] The Ministry of Defense and all subordinate agencies will be included in the restructuring

[172] The government prioritizes increased activity in the north and a more efficient and better protected base structure

[173] The Government will carry out a comprehensive modernization of the support structure in the Armed Forces, including the logistics area, and to a much greater extent base supply and maintenance on deliveries from the civilian market

[174] The use of strategic agreements with civilian suppliers provides benefits such as efficient use of time and resources, increased responsiveness and flexibility, greater operational room for maneuver, improved endurance and increased operational availability

[175] Other agencies in the defense sector

[176] The defense sector consists of the Ministry of Defense and five subordinate agencies

[177] The Norwegian Armed Forces, Defence Materiel, Defence Buildings, Defence Research Institute (FFI) and the National Security Authority (NSM

[178] With the exception of NSM, which also has important tasks that fall under the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, the primary function of the other four agencies is to support the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces

[179] Support for the Armed Forces means that the development of the Armed Forces affects the agencies' missions and tasks

[180] This main mission should be more clearly guiding for the other agencies

[181] The Ministry of Defense and all agencies must continuously work on improvement and efficiency, like all sectors of society

[182] This is both a natural part of a continuous improvement and development process, and also crucial for freeing up resources for prioritized activities

[183] Significant potential for improvement and efficiency gains has been identified within the agencies' areas of responsibility

[184] Personnel and expertise

[185] The competence reform in the defense sector will contribute to the sector's development into a modern competence organization with the right expertise

[186] It is crucial that the sector is able to attract, recruit, utilize, retain and develop the expertise it needs

[187] It is equally important to retrain the skills that are no longer relevant

[188] Conscription is an important prerequisite for the Armed Forces' ability to carry out its tasks

[189] The first-time service will be further developed and better adapted to the Armed Forces' requirements and needs

[190] The government will initiate a reform of the education system that will create better conditions for quality education and more robust academic environments, as well as strengthen research-based education and free up resources for operational activity

[191] The education system must be particularly adapted to the new military system

[192] Other conditions and measures The defense sector conducts research and development (R&D) as part of the development of military capabilities and operational capability

[193] The defense will continue to develop towards a high-tech defense, and key R&D areas will be information and network technology, missile technology, autonomous and unmanned systems, and defense against the same new technology

[194] Further investment will be made in ICT in the defense sector to enable the Armed Forces to perform their most important tasks and to contribute to good utilization of the sector's resources

[195] Preventive security is intended to counter threats to the defense sector's assets and protect them against espionage, sabotage and terrorist acts

[196] This is done through preventive security measures and the detection and handling of security-threatening incidents

[197] The preventive security service in the defense sector shall support the security and defense policy priorities and contribute to increasing the operational capability of the Armed Forces

[198] The Government emphasizes a sustainable defense structure that enables the Armed Forces to fulfill its nine tasks within the specified level of ambition in the short and long term

[199] Deliveries from the defense sector's other agencies are crucial to enabling the Defense Forces to solve these tasks effectively

[200] In parallel with the Armed Forces continuously fulfilling its tasks, the entirety of the measures that follow from this proposition must be realized

[201] It is these two considerations that set the framework for the implementation of the long-term plan and the management of the agencies in the defense sector during the period

[202] In further developing the Armed Forces' overall capabilities, the government will prioritize increased availability and endurance initially in the period

[203] Significantly increased appropriations, modernization and reform will facilitate enhanced responsiveness, increased activity and staffing of selected capacities further in the four-year period

[204] This will also facilitate a continuation and, towards the end of the 2017–2020 period, an escalation of the modernization of several material systems

[205] The Community makes significant resources available to the defense sector, and the government sets high standards for these resources to be managed efficiently and in line with current laws, regulations and political decisions

[206] The defense sector should be characterized by efficient financial management, sound administration, and the ability to continuously innovate and improve

[207] Through the entirety of the measures and goals proposed by the government in this proposal, a solid foundation is established for the long-term development of the defense sector, so that the Armed Forces remain a relevant security policy instrument for Norway
