[355] Part I Framework and guidelines

[356] Norwegian security and defense policy

[357] Norwegian security and defense policy is based on a solid international framework, a strong transatlantic security community through NATO, and society's overall contribution to defense capabilities

[358] Norwegian security is closely linked to international developments

[359] Security and defense policy must enable Norway to respond to challenges across the entire crisis spectrum, from incident management in peacetime, via security policy crises to armed conflict

[360] The armed forces are crucial for safeguarding Norwegian security and for Norway to make credible contributions to collective security

[361] The four other agencies in the defense sector, Defence Construction, Defence Materiel, the Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI) and the National Security Authority (NSM), have their own missions, but all must support the Defence in solving the tasks

[362] The Government will ensure relevant and sustainable defense for the future

[363] A real balance must be created between tasks, structure and finances

[364] The Armed Forces must be organized so that there is a better connection between the tasks assigned to the Armed Forces by the Storting and the government and the tasks that the Armed Forces can solve in practice

[365] Security and defense policy goals

[366] The main purpose of Norwegian security and defense policy is to ensure Norway's sovereignty, territorial integrity and political freedom of action

[367] The cornerstone of Norwegian security policy is the NATO alliance and the transatlantic security community

[368] Norway will contribute to preventing armed conflict and work to ensure that peace and stability are safeguarded within a global, multilateral legal order based on the principles enshrined in the UN Charter

[369] The armed forces are a fundamental and crucial security policy instrument for ensuring Norway's sovereignty and Norwegian rights, and for preserving Norwegian freedom of action

[370] The Armed Forces, together with allies, will contribute to deterrence

[371] The benefits of threatening or challenging Norwegian security should not be in proportion to the costs involved

[372] The Armed Forces shall contribute to ensuring that military threats against Norway do not arise

[373] The Armed Forces, together with allies, shall ensure the collective defense of Norway and allies against threats and attacks

[374] Through participation in international operations and capacity building in selected countries, the Armed Forces shall prevent war and contribute to security and stability

[375] The Armed Forces shall contribute to societal security through support for, and cooperation with, civil authorities in connection with terrorist attacks and other serious incidents, accidents and natural disasters

[376] The formulation of Norwegian security policy is based on a concept of security that encompasses state security, societal security and individual security

[377] The purpose of security policy is to safeguard state security, which means safeguarding the state's sovereignty and integrity, as well as ensuring political freedom of action

[378] The term also includes Norway's contribution to collective defense triggered by the NATO Treaty's Article

[379] Norwegian authorities also have a responsibility to safeguard public security where the safety of the civilian population, central societal functions and infrastructure may be challenged, but without the existence of the state being threatened

[380] Threats to individual and societal security, for example in the form of terrorist attacks and attacks in digital space, can ultimately develop into threats to state security

[381] This emphasizes the need for close security and emergency preparedness cooperation across sector boundaries

[382] The total defense concept encompasses mutual civil-military support across the entire crisis spectrum

[383] Mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society shall contribute to prevention, emergency planning and crisis and consequence management

[384] The need to protect individuals or groups of individuals from genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes can provide a basis for international efforts, including by military means

[385] Security and defense policy priorities

[386] Norwegian security and defense policy must increasingly assume that changes in our security policy environment can occur very quickly

[387] Challenges to European and transatlantic security must be met with cooperation, firmness and predictability

[388] Security policy developments have consequences for our operational ambition, our commitment to the Armed Forces and international cooperation

[389] Norway must be able to take greater responsibility for its own security

[390] The operational capability of the Armed Forces must be strengthened

[391] Based on the security and defense policy goals and development trends described in part

[392] In the proposal, the government has the following priorities for the further development of the Armed Forces

[393] – Strengthen the defense of Norway – Strengthen NATO's collective defense – Contribute to international efforts

[394] – Further develop total defense

[395] Strengthening the defense of Norway

[396] The national defense capability must be strengthened

[397] The defense of Norway takes place within the framework of NATO's collective defense

[398] Close relations with key allies, interoperability, exercises and training, presence and allied support on Norwegian territory or in our immediate area are important for our deterrence capability and for Norwegian and allied defense capabilities in peace, crisis and armed conflict

[399] Norwegian security and defense policy shall strive to ensure that allied reinforcements are in place before a situation develops into a crisis or armed conflict, and that defense efforts can be escalated as seamlessly as possible

[400] However, such early allied involvement cannot be assumed

[401] NATO's collective defense is based on the assumption that all allies have a good ability to defend their own territory, in line with the NATO Treaty's Article

[402] Norway must be able to handle security policy crises, threats and attacks of a certain scale itself, and maintain a level of preparedness that enables us to engage an adversary in all domains

[403] Such a capability, together with a clearly communicated commitment to allied support, will act as a deterrent to a potential adversary

[404] Credible deterrence must therefore be based on more allied exercises and training in peacetime, the ability to receive allied support, and the involvement of allies as early as possible in a crisis

[405] The Norwegian Defence Forces depend on maintaining the ability to understand the situation, conduct intelligence and manage crises

[406] Security policy and technological developments mean that this requires a focus on intelligence and surveillance

[407] Furthermore, the Armed Forces' responsiveness, combat power and endurance will be improved

[408] Better arrangements will be made for allied reinforcements, bilateral and multinational cooperation will be strengthened, and the military presence and exercise and training activities will be increased

[409] Maintaining situational awareness and crisis management capabilities The Armed Forces' daily operations in peacetime form the basis for detecting, averting and, if necessary, handling security policy episodes and crises

[410] The ability to provide timely notification is the starting point for good and rapid decision-making

[411] Good situational awareness in our immediate areas is a prerequisite for being able to make good decisions and for using the Armed Forces in the best possible way

[412] Given the strategic importance of the High North, it is crucial to have a good surveillance capability in order to be able to handle situations that arise, if necessary together with allies

[413] Norway is a maritime nation with responsibility for large ocean areas, and maritime surveillance is a prerequisite for good situational awareness

[414] The intelligence service must maintain its ability to contribute to national authorities having the necessary situational awareness to prevent and handle security incidents and crises, and armed conflict

[415] Due to the demanding technological and security policy developments, it is necessary to invest in intelligence and surveillance to maintain situational awareness

[416] Effective crisis management at the national level requires that strategic decisions are made quickly across sectors, as well as with NATO, the UN and other partners when relevant

[417] The national defense capability depends on a coordinated and practiced crisis management apparatus at all levels to coordinate decisions between different sectors and between political and military levels

[418] Strengthening responsiveness, combat power and endurance The operational capability of the Armed Forces shall be strengthened

[419] Long notice periods can no longer be assumed

[420] Operational capability is a product of responsiveness, combat power and endurance

[421] In order for the Armed Forces to be able to respond sufficiently quickly in a crisis situation, the operational capacities and support functions must be made available in a shorter time than is the case today

[422] Responsiveness is about being able to be in the right place, at the right time and with the right capacity to achieve the desired effect

[423] The armed forces must also have the relevant combat power and endurance to carry out operations over time

[424] Security policy developments are making the challenge more pressing

[425] The Armed Forces have had operational capability for a long time

[426] The response capability, which includes force buildup and movement to areas of operation, is not adapted to the current situation

[427] The Armed Forces must be able to prepare the entire structure within given readiness times and move forces from their bases in a quick and efficient manner

[428] This requires improved logistics preparedness, including through a further developed total defense concept, so that civilian support in the form of goods and services is triggered when needed

[429] The Armed Forces must also strengthen its combat power by maintaining a high level of training, taking advantage of the complementary capabilities of various weapon systems, and continuing to invest in new, relevant capabilities

[430] Combat power is also ensured by building on our interoperability with allies

[431] Furthermore, the Armed Forces' endurance must be strengthened, which places demands on personnel, materiel and logistics, including the ability to maintain supply lines

[432] It must be ensured that Norwegian military power cannot be easily deployed by striking critical infrastructure

[433] It is therefore essential to secure vital objects that are of importance to the defense of Norway throughout the entire crisis spectrum

[434] Active protection measures, military infrastructure, the need for fortification and robust communications infrastructure are measures that reduce vulnerability and support defense capabilities

[435] Threats in the digital space must be detected early

[436] The entire defense sector must be able to implement preventive security measures, and the ability to detect cyber attacks must be improved

[437] The ability to handle such attacks, by implementing relevant countermeasures, will be further developed

[438] Facilitate Allied reinforcements

[439] Reinforcing Norway with allied forces has been an important prerequisite in Norwegian security policy and strategy throughout the post-war period

[440] An active alliance policy is therefore fundamentally important

[441] The security policy developments and increased military activity in our immediate areas make it more important to link NATO and close allies more closely to Norway and Norwegian interests, both in everyday life, in crises and in conflict

[442] The United States is Norway's most important ally and the bilateral relationship is of great importance to Norwegian security

[443] The agreements on American pre-storage have great security policy and operational value and are therefore particularly significant

[444] The solution is also cost-effective, both for the US and for Norway

[445] These agreements must be continued, further developed and harmonized with allied and national plans, which must be practiced and trained

[446] Conditions must be created so that allied support can be quickly deployed in the event of a threat of armed conflict and before a security crisis escalates

[447] This requires good national and allied planning, clear decision-making responsibility and clear command and control relationships

[448] In the event of a serious security crisis or armed conflict, Norway must have sufficient capacity to effectively receive and support allied reinforcement forces so that they can participate in operations

[449] A focus on operational cooperation with allied reinforcement forces is crucial for defense capability

[450] Strengthen bilateral and multinational cooperation

[451] Norway must prioritize operational and security policy cooperation with selected allies that are relevant for bilateral and allied reinforcement of Norway in security policy crises and armed conflict

[452] Ongoing cooperation with close allies is also becoming increasingly important in order to collaborate on contributions to international crisis management

[453] Cooperation will increasingly be a prerequisite for acquiring, operating and maintaining capabilities that Norway needs, as well as for ensuring the ability to operate together

[454] In addition to further developing the relationship with our most important ally, the United States, Norway will also strengthen the binding bilateral and multinational cooperation with close European allies such as the United Kingdom, Germany, France and the Netherlands

[455] The Northern European countries constitute a significant community of security and military interests that supports broader cooperation within NATO

[456] The Northern European security and defense policy dialogue in the Northern Group is important as a forum for information exchange and confidence-building between the countries in the region

[457] It is important to participate in multinational cooperation forums within the alliance, such as the British-led

[458] Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) and the German-led Framework Nations Concept (FNC

[459] Cooperation with other NATO allies and partner countries is prioritized where this is in Norway's interest

[460] The further development of the Nordic Defence Cooperation (NORDEFCO) continues in areas that provide security policy, capacity and operational benefits

[461] Multinational cooperation is an important tool for further developing military capabilities and giving Norway access to capabilities that are too resource-intensive to realize on its own

[462] Security policy developments, technological developments and the need for cost-effective solutions underpin the need to strengthen the focus on multinational defence cooperation through more and more integrated cooperation solutions

[463] Multinational cooperation is demanding and often encounters several obstacles and objections

[464] Different national needs and interests can sometimes be difficult to reconcile

[465] Varying military traditions and practices, in addition to conflicting industrial interests, are among the biggest challenges to finding good solutions

[466] Collaboration can also challenge more traditional notions of national sovereignty and operational autonomy

[467] However, these are interests and perceptions that must be challenged if collaboration is to succeed

[468] A strengthened focus on cooperation means that the capabilities and activities of the defense sector must be assessed in a multinational perspective

[469] Agencies and branches of defense shall, to the greatest extent possible, be further developed in cooperation with close allies

[470] Exceptions will only be applicable in cases where national ownership and control of the capability is crucial, or where the activity is not naturally suitable for collaboration

[471] The collaboration will be based on thorough analyses and early dialogue with relevant partners

[472] Defense planning, operational planning, structural development, investments, research and development, exercises and training must be seen in light of opportunities for multinational cooperation

[473] The Norwegian side must demonstrate a willingness to adapt specific national requirements

[474] A similar willingness must be shown from relevant partners if the collaboration is to be successful

[475] Increased military presence and more exercises and training Norwegian security and defense policy must emphasize relevant military presence in the land, sea and air domains

[476] Regular presence in the form of daily operations communicates Norwegian interests, ensures the necessary political and military situational awareness, and provides shorter warning and reaction times

[477] It is therefore important to prioritize military presence with relevant operational capabilities in our immediate areas, especially in the north, to create predictability and stability

[478] Peacetime presence is maintained through a combination of operational activity and exercises and training with national, multinational and allied forces

[479] Presence over time requires that the Armed Forces have relevant bases and relevant infrastructure, as well as good exercise and training areas in strategically and operationally important areas

[480] Exercises and training, also together with allied forces, are an important security policy tool for Norway

[481] Regular allied exercises and training in peacetime maintain a normal situation with an allied presence in Norway that has a stabilizing and predictable effect

[482] This provides joint training and helps strengthen the interoperability on which allied operations depend

[483] This also helps provide allies with valuable knowledge of and the ability to operate in areas close to Norway

[484] The government is planning more allied exercises and training on Norwegian territory

[485] Norway must provide sufficient infrastructure and host nation support for allied exercises and training

[486] Allied presence in Norwegian areas of responsibility is managed in accordance with Norwegian base policy

[487] Strengthen NATO's collective defence

[488] NATO must have the necessary political will and military combat power to deter a potential adversary from threatening or attacking the alliance's member countries

[489] It is therefore an overarching priority to strengthen NATO's collective defence (Article 5) by contributing to NATO as a defence alliance and as a transatlantic security policy consultation forum

[490] The revitalization of NATO's collective defense capability is in line with Norway's long-term priorities and will continue to be central to Norway's work towards NATO

[491] Continued American engagement and presence in Europe is important

[492] The security policy situation emphasizes the importance of better transatlantic burden sharing – politically, militarily and economically – by European countries increasing their defense budgets and contributing relevant capabilities to solve military tasks both within and outside the alliance area

[493] Norway will emphasize contributing its share of NATO's overall capabilities so that the alliance is able to fulfill its tasks, as well as helping to follow up on the decisions from the Wales Summit on the Readiness Action Plan, reassurance measures and long-term adaptation of the alliance with relevant contributions

[494] It is a goal for Norway to contribute regularly and substantially to NATO's standing forces and contingency forces with a planning horizon of five years

[495] This is done to contribute to both operational and financial predictability

[496] NATO is updating its geographic contingency plans, including plans for Norway and the maritime flanks

[497] Regular allied activity, exercises and training on Norwegian territory are relevant for deterrence and collective defense

[498] This will be the framework when Norway hosts NATO's

[499] High Visibility Exercise

[500] A prepared and practiced plan improves NATO's ability to act quickly in a crisis situation and also has an important political function because it demonstrates the Alliance's will and ability for collective defense of its member countries

[501] NATO's rapid reaction forces are intended to be an instrument to demonstrate and lend credibility to the Alliance's ability and willingness to act with military force throughout the Alliance's area

[502] Norway will actively contribute to strengthening the alliance by improving situational awareness for the entire alliance area in NATO's command structure

[503] Contributions to strengthening the connection between NATO's command structure and national headquarters will be an important part of this

[504] Contribute to international efforts

[505] The Armed Forces must maintain their ability to engage in international efforts

[506] International developments indicate that the great need for international efforts for peace, security and stability, both in the form of international operations and capacity building, will persist

[507] Such support can include security sector reform to improve a country's ability to ensure its own security, but can also include peace and stabilization operations

[508] It is in Norway's interest to contribute to maintaining international peace and security

[509] International efforts within an allied framework are an investment in solidarity that ensures that Norway also receives allied support if we need it

[510] In addition to participation in international operations, international efforts include several types of exercises and training abroad, participation in force registers, reassurance measures and capacity building

[511] Norway will particularly seek to make capacity building a cost-effective contribution to international efforts, preferably in multinational frameworks

[512] The Norwegian Armed Forces' ability to handle the upper part of the crisis spectrum in Norwegian areas means that we have relevant capacities for international contributions

[513] The extent of such participation must, however, be seen in light of the availability of personnel and equipment and the need for national preparedness

[514] Further develop total defense

[515] Total Defence encompasses mutual civil-military support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society, and shall contribute to prevention, emergency planning and crisis and consequence management across the entire crisis spectrum

[516] In a serious crisis situation and in armed conflict, the Armed Forces' need for civilian support in the form of materiel, goods, services and access to infrastructure will exceed what the Armed Forces have at their disposal on a daily basis

[517] There is a need to further develop total defense so that society's combined resources can be mobilized for the defense of the country, if necessary

[518] Civilian support is absolutely necessary to maintain and further develop relevant defense capabilities

[519] The support from civil society, together with the capabilities of the Armed Forces, must be able to support the entire national force structure and allied reinforcement forces simultaneously

[520] Total defense is designed in accordance with international law by separating military activities to the necessary extent from civilian groups and objects worthy of protection

[521] The Armed Forces also play an important role as a support resource for civilian emergency response agencies, which has gained increasing importance in recent years

[522] The Armed Forces' ability to assist civil authorities in the event of natural disasters, accidents, terrorist attacks and other serious crimes will be further developed

[523] Strengthening the Armed Forces' operational capability will also provide a stronger ability to assist in civilian crisis management, thereby improving society's overall preparedness

[524] Mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society are discussed in more detail in Chapter 4. 1.4 The tasks of the Armed Forces

[525] The Defence Policy defines the framework and overall guidelines for the development of the Armed Forces by specifying the tasks and ambitions of the Armed Forces, and the direction for structural planning and the development of operational capability

[526] This is an operationalization of the security and defense policy goals and is intended to ensure development so that Norway has a defense that can safeguard Norwegian and allied security at all times

[527] The composition of the Armed Forces' tasks will continue as decided by the Storting in Recommendation

[528] St (2011–2012) to Prop

[529] It is important to have continuity in the task set, but the description of the tasks has been updated in light of security policy developments and the government's priorities

[530] The tasks of the Armed Forces are the Storting's and the Government's overall mission to the Armed Forces

[531] The structure and operational capacities of the Armed Forces must be developed to be able to carry out missions within their framework

[532] Each of the Armed Forces' tasks is accompanied by a text describing the task's content and level of ambition

[533] The entirety of these frameworks and guidelines constitute the tasks of the Armed Forces

[534] The tasks are summarized as follows

[535] Ensure credible deterrence based on NATO's collective defense Defend Norway and allies against serious threats, attacks and attacks, within the framework of NATO's collective defense Prevent and handle incidents and security policy crises with national resources, including facilitating allied engagement Ensure a national basis for decision-making through surveillance and intelligence

[536] Asserted Norwegian sovereignty and sovereign rights

[537] Maintain the exercise of authority in defined areas Participate in multinational crisis management, including peace operations Contribute to international cooperation in the area of security and defense policy Contribute to the maintenance of public security and other central societal tasks

[538] expresses the most central function of the Armed Forces

[539] The defense must deter potential aggressors and prevent conflicts involving the use of military means from arising

[540] If necessary, Norway, together with allies, must be able to defend Norwegian and allied territory, as expressed in tasks 2 and

[541] Some of the Armed Forces' tasks originate from national responsibilities and interests related to Norway and its surrounding areas

[542] These tasks must primarily be solved with national resources

[543] Tasks 3–6 are all tasks that fall under this category

[544] Other tasks must be solved in cooperation with others and primarily with our allies in NATO

[545] Tasks 1, 2 and 7 are included in this category

[546] Task 8 is most often linked to cooperation with allies, while Task 9 is basically a national task, although it may also require cooperation across national borders

[547] Tasks 1-7 are dimensioning for the Armed Forces

[548] This means that the Armed Forces must be equipped, manned and led specifically to solve these tasks

[549] At the same time, support for civil society should be a greater determinant of the organization and dimensioning of certain capacities in the Armed Forces

[550] This is relevant, among other things, when designing dedicated missions, emergency preparedness orders, localization, requirements for training, exercises and practice, as well as the ability to collaborate with actors outside the Armed Forces

[551] The total defense concept today encompasses mutual civil-military support across the entire crisis spectrum from incident management in peacetime to crisis and armed conflict

[552] The government is further developing total defense so that society's overall resources can be mobilized to a greater extent in the event of a security crisis and armed conflict

[553] Task 9 describes which capabilities the Armed Forces can contribute to support civilian authorities, and which are specifically designed for this purpose

[554] The overall level of ambition for the Armed Forces' tasks is confirmed mainly through the description of the individual tasks

[555] The content of the task is described along with the key capabilities that the Armed Forces need to solve the tasks

[556] These capabilities are also important for the Armed Forces' organization and structure to be developed in line with security and defense policy goals and priorities

[557] The organisation and structure of the Armed Forces are described in more detail in chapter

[558] Ensuring credible deterrence based on NATO's collective defense The ability of the Armed Forces to solve its tasks, alone and together with allies, constitutes the overall defense capability

[559] The fact that the costs of carrying or attacking Norway's security, territory or political freedom of action become unacceptably high constitutes a deterrent effect

[560] The ability to handle military challenges should help prevent threats from arising

[561] Credible deterrence is ensured through an active alliance policy that is predictable, long-term and conflict-preventive

[562] NATO is the core of Norway's ability for credible deterrence

[563] Since NATO was founded, the organization's primary purpose has been to prevent armed conflict through a clear ability and willingness to defend the alliance by military means if necessary

[564] The Norwegian Armed Forces shall contribute to ensuring that NATO remains credible in our immediate vicinity

[565] This requires the ability to react immediately, effectively and with relevant means if Norway is exposed to pressure, threats or attacks, as well as the ability to cooperate with allied forces within the framework of NATO's collective defense

[566] The Armed Forces must be able to meet a number of challenges

[567] The most demanding challenges involve the Armed Forces having the ability to conduct high-intensity combat operations over time in a national or allied joint operational framework

[568] Rapid decisions based on early warning are important for the Armed Forces to be able to immediately meet challenges

[569] Early warning requires that the Armed Forces must have the ability to establish and maintain situational awareness throughout the Norwegian immediate area

[570] Even though certain capabilities appear to be particularly central from a deterrence perspective, such as submarines, air defense and a modern combat aircraft, the Norwegian contribution to conflict prevention in our immediate areas will not primarily consist of individual capabilities, but of the Armed Forces' overall resources

[571] The Armed Forces must therefore have the ability to coordinate efforts with several relevant capacities simultaneously

[572] Furthermore, the Armed Forces must be able to protect their own military facilities and military equipment to ensure availability in a given situation

[573] Presence through regular exercises and training, as well as permanent Norwegian bases, demonstrates the ability and willingness to defend the country

[574] The Armed Forces must therefore conduct regular exercises and training throughout the Norwegian vicinity and facilitate exercises and training with allies

[575] This contributes to stability and predictability in our local areas

[576] Task

[577] Defend Norway and allies against serious threats, attacks, within the framework of NATO's collective defense. NATO is the framework for the collective defense of Norway and our allies

[578] The Norwegian Armed Forces, together with our allies, will handle threats, attacks and threats against Norway and other NATO countries and prevent hostile actors from establishing themselves on Norwegian or our allies' territory or challenging our sovereignty

[579] This includes both state and non-state actors that cause or threaten to cause such extensive damage that it is appropriate for NATO to implement collective defense measures

[580] Defense of Norwegian territory against serious threats, attacks and attacks is carried out as integrated allied joint operations led by NATO, where Norwegian forces are part of a broad allied effort

[581] Allied operations will be led by the NATO command structure

[582] The Norwegian Armed Forces' command and control structure must be able to interact with this and at the same time be capable of effective management of national forces that are not assigned to NATO

[583] Interoperability and the ability to cooperate with NATO's command structure and other allied force contributions are therefore crucial

[584] The Armed Forces must arrange for the reception and support of allied reinforcements

[585] Plans for receiving allied reinforcements must be kept updated, practiced and trained

[586] The armed forces must also have the ability to protect the infrastructure required to receive such reinforcements

[587] The collective defense obligation is mutual, and due to the security situation, NATO has strengthened cooperation on preparedness and standing forces

[588] Norway contributes actively and the Armed Forces must be able to provide Norwegian forces for collective defense in other NATO countries

[589] The starting point for Norwegian participation is forces that are registered with NATO's response forces, NATO's standing maritime forces and air forces on special alert

[590] National contributions to these forces are important for NATO countries to be able to maintain a high level of readiness and good defense capabilities

[591] The Armed Forces must have the ability to move their contributions to the relevant area of operation

[592] Norway will strive to provide relevant Norwegian force contributions together with our closest allies

[593] The Army should be able to contribute regularly to NATO's response forces and the Navy should be able to contribute regularly to NATO's standing maritime forces, including occasionally being able to lead such forces

[594] The Air Force shall regularly contribute units or individual platforms from the entire air defense structure

[595] The Air Force's ability to contribute combat aircraft will be limited during a transitional period until the F-35 is phased in

[596] The Armed Forces' special forces will be able to provide independent force contributions at times

[597] If collective defense in NATO is implemented, Norwegian force contributions can be increased beyond this

[598] The force contributions must have the ability to participate in and conduct high-intensity combat operations over time within an allied joint operational framework

[599] Task

[600] Prevent and handle incidents and security policy crises with national resources, including facilitating allied engagement

[601] The Armed Forces must be able to handle security policy crises and projections of a certain magnitude

[602] Episodes and crises that are handled nationally should be brought under control, possibly in parallel with Norwegian authorities involving the alliance

[603] Although major military challenges must be handled with allied reinforcements, the Armed Forces must be able to meet threats in a credible and relevant manner, even before allies are involved

[604] Crisis management operations must be able to seamlessly transition to collective defense

[605] The ability to establish and maintain situational awareness in Norwegian areas is a prerequisite for being able to respond to crises in an effective manner

[606] Good situational awareness within the land, sea, air and cyber domains is necessary to ensure a timely and sound decision-making basis

[607] Relevant military presence is also of great importance, as this highlights Norwegian interests and strengthens the ability to handle incidents and crises up to a certain level without deploying additional military capabilities

[608] Various crisis situations require flexible capacities with good responsiveness and may result in the Armed Forces having to engage an adversary militarily to protect Norwegian sovereignty

[609] Military operations require a necessary degree of control in the land, sea and air domains, and a national defense must have the ability to establish this degree of control

[610] Furthermore, military operations will require access to the cyber domain and control of their own information infrastructure

[611] A crisis or armed conflict can last for a long time, and the ability to provide logistical support is therefore critical to the Armed Forces' operational capability

[612] A crisis or armed conflict situation requires the ability to lead joint operations at both the operational and tactical levels, as well as the ability to cooperate with civilian actors

[613] A crisis can affect multiple parts of society and challenge the nation's ability for cross-sectoral crisis management

[614] The Armed Forces depend on support from and close cooperation with civil society to carry out a number of the Armed Forces' tasks

[615] Rapid strategic decisions are essential for effective utilization of the Armed Forces' ability to avert and manage incidents and security policy crises

[616] Ensuring a national decision-making basis through surveillance and intelligence

[617] The Armed Forces must have the independent ability to conduct intelligence in order to establish and maintain situational awareness in Norwegian areas of interest

[618] The Armed Forces' surveillance and intelligence activities shall maintain a good situational understanding, as a basis for timely decisions by political authorities and the Armed Forces' leadership

[619] The task therefore requires a unified intelligence capacity in the Armed Forces from strategic to tactical levels

[620] Through its surveillance and intelligence activities, Norway must be able to provide timely warning of situations and developments that are of importance to Norwegian sovereignty and Norwegian interests

[621] Norway must have an independent ability to conduct intelligence in its own immediate areas, including in the land, sea, air and cyber domains

[622] The entire operational structure of the Armed Forces must be able to contribute to collecting, summarizing, analyzing and disseminating information

[623] The national intelligence capacity shall also support operations at home and abroad at the operational and tactical level

[624] Effective monitoring of Norwegian areas of interest and close proximity is not only a prerequisite for the Armed Forces to be able to carry out its other tasks, but it is also a key contribution to a good situational understanding in NATO

[625] This is a significant Norwegian contribution to the alliance

[626] Norway must therefore have the ability to effectively exchange intelligence of importance to Norway, NATO and other partner countries

[627] Within the framework of NATO's integrated air defense, the Armed Forces must be able to continuously monitor Norwegian airspace and adjacent areas

[628] The Armed Forces must also have the ability to monitor selected activity in the territorial sea, including underwater and in selected geographical areas at sea where Norway has jurisdiction

[629] The Navy and Air Force regularly contribute to such monitoring, and if necessary, different capacities can be combined for continuous real-time monitoring of delimited sea areas

[630] The Armed Forces must have the ability to conduct continuous real-time surveillance in parts of the country's territory, primarily along the border with Russia, where the Border Guard has an important role

[631] The Armed Forces must also have the ability to conduct intelligence and surveillance in the digital space

[632] The Armed Forces must be able to exchange information and assessments with other agencies and sectors in accordance with established regulations, as well as with allies and partners

[633] Task

[634] Asserted Norwegian sovereignty and sovereign rights

[635] The defense forces must assert Norwegian sovereignty and protect Norway's interests

[636] This includes preventing unlawful interventions by states and non-state actors that directly or indirectly challenge Norwegian sovereignty or Norwegian sovereign rights

[637] The Armed Forces must be able to handle limited incidents, prevent unauthorized actors from gaining access to Norwegian territory, and prevent vital societal interests from being put at risk

[638] The task also includes securing Norwegian foreign missions and Norwegian shipping when necessary

[639] The Armed Forces must be able to handle various types of violations of Norwegian sovereignty at short notice, even when several such situations arise simultaneously

[640] The armed forces must have sufficient resources to both monitor activity in nearby Norwegian areas and to be able to be present at short notice with suitable units prepared to exercise coercive power on land, at sea and in the air if necessary

[641] Through its presence in priority sea areas, the Coast Guard has an important function in asserting sovereignty at sea

[642] In the airspace, the task is carried out within the framework of NATO's integrated air defense, where the Armed Forces contribute with air surveillance and fighter aircraft that are on continuous alert

[643] Through its presence and information gathering, the Border Guard has the ability to respond to violations of Norwegian sovereignty along the Norwegian-Russian border

[644] Furthermore, HM provides

[645] The King's Guard routinely guards and secures the royal house

[646] Task

[647] Maintain the exercise of authority in limited areas. The exercise of authority is the enforcement of legal orders, prohibitions and conditions directed at individuals or other private actors

[648] This is a national task that is normally carried out by the police and other civilian authorities, but in two main areas the Armed Forces are assigned special authority and responsibility

[649] Resource control and other exercise of authority at sea, as well as border surveillance along the Norwegian-Russian border

[650] This also includes preventive measures

[651] The Armed Forces fulfill their role in these fields in close cooperation with other public agencies

[652] The exercise of authority in the North will be a key task for the Armed Forces in the years ahead

[653] Potential consequences of continued ice melting in the Arctic, such as possible increased activity and resource exploitation in the area, could reinforce this

[654] The Armed Forces must therefore have the ability to quickly detect and respond to violations of Norwegian laws and regulations in the areas where the Armed Forces are granted such authority

[655] This exercise of authority must be sufficiently clear and consistent to have a preventive effect against actors who deliberately challenge Norwegian laws and regulations

[656] In the fisheries sector, this involves the ability to exercise resource control through effective monitoring, relevant presence and regular inspections in all areas where catching and fishing take place

[657] This applies particularly to areas with high activity, both in the highlands and in the North Sea

[658] The Coast Guard exercises authority in the Norwegian economic zone, the fishing zone at Jan Mayen and the fish protection zone around Svalbard, and is supported by surveillance from satellites, aircraft, helicopters and other military vessels

[659] The Border Guard has a military role

[660] In addition, the level of ambition for the Border Guard reflects Norway's international obligations in the Schengen cooperation and is based on complementary measures, including the ability for continuous surveillance, routine patrolling and situational responses in cooperation with the police and the Border Commissioner

[661] Task

[662] Participate in multinational crisis management, including peace operations

[663] The international challenges indicate that there will be a need for international efforts for peace, security and stability in the years ahead

[664] The Armed Forces must have the ability to contribute relevant capabilities abroad, including in multinational exercises, reassurance measures, capacity building, preventive stabilization operations, more traditional peacekeeping operations and peace-building operations

[665] Such contributions are part of the shared responsibility for peace and security

[666] Norway must join in and support

[667] The scope of international efforts must be assessed against availability and the need for national preparedness

[668] Norwegian forces will normally contribute within a multilateral framework, in which NATO and the UN will be the most important actors

[669] Norway should also have the military capacity to contribute to EU or coalition operations

[670] Norwegian participation in multinational crisis management must be based on international law

[671] The gender perspective must be taken into account in all international efforts, in line with UN Resolution 1325 on women, peace and security and the government's action plan in the area

[672] The protection of civilians must be seen in this context

[673] Within a force structure with a limited scope, as many of the Armed Forces' capabilities as possible must be usable both at home and abroad

[674] For this to be possible, Norwegian units and all permanently employed military personnel, as well as certain categories of civilians, must, as a general rule, be available for missions both nationally and abroad

[675] Norwegian forces must be able to cooperate effectively with allied forces and partners in international missions

[676] This places demands on mobility, firepower and self-protection

[677] Furthermore, the Armed Forces must be able to provide forces for international operations at short notice and at the same time have sufficient endurance to stand with allies and partners in an operational area over time

[678] In order to have such endurance, the Armed Forces must draw on contributions from all branches of defense and joint capabilities

[679] Burden sharing within the Armed Forces must be strived for in such operations

[680] The Army, Navy and Air Force should be able to deliver mission-adapted force contributions, smaller units or individual platforms for a period within a multinational framework

[681] The Armed Forces' special forces must be able to contribute independent forces

[682] The joint departments, including logistics and support, must be able to support the forces to the extent described above, in up to three operations or three geographically separate operational areas simultaneously

[683] The armed forces must have access to strategic mobility to be able to quickly deploy or withdraw forces

[684] The Armed Forces must also be able to assume national medical responsibility for Norwegian personnel participating in military operations abroad

[685] Contribute to international cooperation in the area of security and defense policy

[686] The Armed Forces shall contribute support to international military cooperation as part of the work to create peace and stability, including the work to prevent weapons of mass destruction and associated means of delivery from becoming available to actors who pose a potential threat to Norwegian and international security

[687] This includes measures such as information gathering, analysis, arms control, confidence-building activities and verification

[688] Furthermore, the task includes training in and contributions to security sector reform and capacity building in selected countries

[689] This will contribute to building the partners' ability to contribute to international security and international cooperation, as well as the ability to reform and ensure democratic control over their own defense sectors

[690] The Armed Forces coordinate the required military contributions to international cooperation in the area of ​​security and defense policy, and the entire defense sector should be able to contribute to its implementation

[691] The effort is aimed at safeguarding Norway's international obligations and is carried out through military representation at a number of Norwegian foreign missions and in military headquarters, as a follow-up to the bilateral and multilateral cooperation agreements the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces have established with a number of countries

[692] In addition, visits, exchanges of personnel and specific cooperation activities are carried out at various levels

[693] The intelligence service's collection and assessments and the Armed Forces' active follow-up of agreements on disarmament and confidence-building measures are also important

[694] Task

[695] Contribute to safeguarding public safety and other key societal tasks

[696] The Armed Forces contribute to societal security in a number of areas, based on the total defense concept

[697] The concept is based on the principle of mutual civil-military support and cooperation across the entire crisis spectrum from peace via security policy crisis to armed conflict

[698] The total defense concept therefore encompasses both military support for civil society and civilian support for the Armed Forces, and is effective in addressing challenges to societal security as well as state security

[699] The Armed Forces, as part of the total defense system, should be able to support civil society in preventing, preparing for emergencies, managing crises and dealing with the consequences of terrorist attacks and other serious crimes, accidents and natural disasters

[700] The Armed Forces' contribution to societal security also provides a better ability to safeguard Norwegian national security because a functioning civil society and robust societal security are important foundations for a functioning military defense

[701] The Armed Forces depend on society functioning as normally as possible, even in times of crisis and armed conflict

[702] The Armed Forces' assistance is provided upon request and is normally relevant when the civilian authorities, who have primary responsibility for safeguarding public security, do not have sufficient resources to handle the situation

[703] All available resources of the Armed Forces should be able to assist in civilian crisis management, depending on the actual situation and the needs of civilian authorities

[704] Nevertheless, the Armed Forces must first and foremost prioritize their primary military tasks

[705] These are tasks that only the Armed Forces are capable of carrying out

[706] Military capabilities should not be tied to civil preparedness in a way that goes beyond military preparedness

[707] Some of the Armed Forces' capabilities are particularly relevant and specifically geared towards assisting civil society within search and rescue services and in a terrorist situation

[708] The Armed Forces' special forces and the Armed Forces' helicopter capacity have dedicated missions and preparedness, which means that the civilian authorities' need for assistance is partly decisive for the organization, equipment, staffing and training of these capacities

[709] This also applies to some extent to the Home Guard

[710] In addition to assistance to societal security at the request of civilian authorities, the Armed Forces also ensures ongoing contributions to key societal tasks in several areas as a significant part of its portfolio

[711] These tasks affect the organization and activity of the units

[712] Examples of this are the Coast Guard, the Border Guard, HM the King's Guard and the Intelligence Service

[713] In these areas, the Armed Forces provide significant support to civil society on a daily basis

[714] Principles for the design of the defense structure

[715] The Government bases its recommendation on the further development of the defense sector on four principles

[716] Firstly, a real balance must be created between tasks, structure and finances

[717] A historic strengthening of the funding level is crucial to ensure this

[718] But even with a significantly increased financial framework, structural changes and further efficiency improvements are also necessary to meet changing operational needs and so that the community's resources are directed to an even greater extent than today towards the most important tasks and capacities

[719] The Government takes into account more precise and realistic calculations of cost developments for the capacities included in the recommended structure than have been the basis for previous long-term plans

[720] Secondly, the government emphasizes that changes in the Armed Forces should take place within a comprehensive framework

[721] In a modern, network-based defense, defense capability consists of more than the sum of the capacities of individual elements

[722] Ensuring a balance within the Armed Forces so that the various structural elements provide a mutually reinforcing effect is therefore necessary to achieve the greatest possible defense capability within the financial framework

[723] The composition of the structure that constitutes a balanced defense depends on a number of factors that are constantly changing

[724] It must be considered regardless of the relative size of the defense branches

[725] A comprehensive framework must therefore guide the choice of capacities and locations

[726] The alternative is that the defense structure becomes the sum of accumulated, isolated decisions

[727] Then the possibility of collaboration and mutual reinforcement between the different capacities will be dictated by considerations other than operational ones

[728] Thirdly, it is a key objective for the government to ensure a better connection between what the Armed Forces are expected to be able to do and what the Armed Forces can actually do

[729] The government therefore emphasizes increased realism in defense planning, so that operational capability, availability, and preparedness are truly strengthened

[730] Structure tables are of little help if the strengths cannot actually be used for what they are expected to do

[731] Large investments in military capabilities, which are not utilized optimally for economic reasons, also contribute to weakening the credibility of the Armed Forces

[732] Some of the biggest challenges in today's Defence are related to operations and are reflected in inadequate maintenance and emergency logistics, as well as lack of staffing, presence, training and exercises

[733] These challenges have been building up over a long period of time

[734] One of the biggest financial promises in this long-term plan will be that higher and more realistic operating costs will be included for staffing, activities, rehearsals and training

[735] This is also one of the most important measures for the Armed Forces to actually be able to solve the tasks that society expects it to do

[736] Rather than continuing the structure or acquiring systems that cannot in practice be operated in a way that provides real operational capability, the government recommends using resources on staffing, maintenance and training of prioritized capacities

[737] Fourth, decisions must be substantiated in a long-term perspective

[738] In a modern defense, all decisions about personnel, materiel and infrastructure are so costly and long-term that the costs over the entire service life must be planned for

[739] One-sided concentration on the next decision or the four-year period, without seeing it in a holistic and long-term perspective, increases the likelihood of misinvestments

[740] The long-term cost picture must be carefully assessed in connection with large investments, and investment costs in a shorter perspective must be seen in the context of the gain in operational capability over time

[741] The government has therefore considered the short-term as well as a more long-term cost picture, and realistic costs over the entire lifetime of the capacities have been taken as a basis

[742] Framework conditions and trends

[743] The framework conditions for Norwegian security have deteriorated since the previous long-term plan for the defense sector was prepared

[744] The security situation in our part of the world is, in sum, more demanding than it has been in a long time

[745] Major challenges close to NATO's area of responsibility can have direct consequences for Norwegian and allied security

[746] These are in addition to challenges in European countries and already existing security challenges related to global developments

[747] The major challenges indicate that Norway and allied countries must strengthen their defense capabilities

[748] General societal trends also have an impact on the Armed Forces

[749] Security and defense policy developments are influenced by political, technological, economic and demographic developments and by climate change

[750] This requires adaptability at all levels in the sector and for long-term defense planning

[751] Global trends The world's economic center of gravity is changing

[752] States with growing economies are challenging the position of Western countries in international politics

[753] This contributes to a global, as well as regional, power shift

[754] Some emerging powers are characterized by authoritarian governance, market economies and strengthened military capabilities, which together may appear to some states as an alternative to democratic values

[755] Economic and political developments create room for great power rivalry

[756] Violations of international law and disagreements about goals and means in international cooperation for peace and stability undermine international security

[757] These global developments will likely shape the world for a long time to come, and will also affect Norwegian areas and interests

[758] Norwegian interests are not served by international rules being challenged or broken by actors who put power before law

[759] The security policy situation is becoming increasingly complex and unpredictable, and changes can occur quickly and without clear warning

[760] Europe Europe is changing

[761] The combination of demanding internal and external developments puts pressure on politics, the economy, solidarity and the ability to meet profound challenges with good and effective instruments

[762] The largest refugee crisis since World War II comes on top of economic and social challenges that already exist in many European countries

[763] Political polarization, radicalization, and extremism on our own continent are reinforced by social and political developments and the influence of external actors

[764] Europe faces significant challenges that directly and indirectly affect security policy

[765] The ability to make good decisions and the ability to come together around common courses of action that benefit everyone is put under pressure by the complex challenge landscape

[766] The EU and NATO have long been the central international forums for close and ongoing cooperation between the countries in the region, thus contributing to stability

[767] NATO's role and development, together with the United States' continued involvement in NATO, are crucial for European security

[768] The alliance is a clear expression of the transatlantic relationship and the importance of the United States to European security

[769] Russia's increased military capability and use of force constitute the most central change in Norway's security policy environment since the previous long-term plan

[770] Through the war in Georgia in 2008, the illegal annexation of Crimea in the spring of 2014, and the destabilization of Eastern Ukraine, Russian rulers have over time demonstrated the willingness and ability to use a wide range of instruments, including military force, to maintain political dominance and influence

[771] Russian security strategies and military doctrines show that the authorities want influence in Russian neighboring areas

[772] This particularly involves preventing further NATO expansion eastward and the establishment of bases and deployment of military equipment in these areas

[773] Russian leaders express a lack of trust in Western countries' intentions, particularly regarding NATO's role in the Baltics and Eastern Europe

[774] Russian authorities also express dissatisfaction with Western countries' lack of consideration in areas Moscow considers its legitimate "sphere of interest

[775] In this way, Russia contributes to undermining the right of independent states to self-determination

[776] Russia's ambition is to re-establish the country as a great power

[777] Militarily, this implies a Russian ambition to have a credible regional and global strategic deterrence capability with nuclear weapons, as well as sufficient conventional capability to avoid or manage a conflict

[778] Russia's use of military force in Syria illustrates its global great power ambitions and strategic interests in the Middle East

[779] Not since the withdrawal from Afghanistan in 1989 has Russia conducted military operations outside the former Soviet territory

[780] Through the military reform initiated in 2008, Russia has invested heavily in military power

[781] The political will to prioritize defense has continued despite the economic downturn

[782] The significant strengthening of the country's military capability has been demonstrated through exercises and military operations

[783] Modernization will likely continue to strengthen Russian conventional military capabilities in the future

[784] Russia has strengthened its nuclear weapons capability, which has played an important role in the Russian defense concept for many years

[785] Military response capability has been strengthened through increased ability to rapidly move forces, higher readiness for parts of the military structure, and streamlining of the command and control structure

[786] This significantly reduces Russian reaction time and potentially very short warning time for the opposing party in a potential conflict

[787] The reaction time depends on the type of intervention, but can vary from weeks to less than hours

[788] Over the next decade, the Russian military will have several types of cruise missiles with long range, high precision, and high penetration capability

[789] The long-range precision weapons enable Russia to carry out attacks from great distances and with short notice

[790] Russia does not currently pose a military threat to Norway

[791] Nevertheless, Russia's military development reinforces the asymmetry in relations with Norway

[792] The combination of Russian military development and a more unpredictable political behavior means that Russia is still a central factor in Norwegian defense planning

[793] Russia does not consider Norway to be part of its so-called "sphere of interest

[794] Russian actions in Ukraine therefore do not have a direct transfer value to Norwegian conditions

[795] Nevertheless, the Russian approach, with combinations of overt and covert, military and non-military means, could be representative of how Russia might act in a complex crisis also in our immediate vicinity

[796] A potential crisis will probably not start in Norway's immediate vicinity, but could have consequences there

[797] Given the strained relationship between NATO and Russia, it is crucial to avoid misunderstandings

[798] To safeguard security in the sea areas in the north and ensure stability and predictability in our immediate areas, the government has therefore maintained the direct line between the Norwegian Armed Forces' Operational Headquarters (FOH) and the Russian Northern Fleet, cooperation within the coast guard and border guard, cooperation on search and rescue, and the mechanisms in the Incidents at Sea Agreement

[799] To counteract continued negative developments between Russia and NATO and avoid misunderstandings in connection with exercises and training, it is important to continue and update existing agreements and establish new mechanisms that contribute to transparency and predictability of military activity

[800] The Vienna Document, the Open Skies Treaty and the Conventional Forces in Europe (CFE) Treaty are such existing mechanisms

[801] However, Russia unilaterally suspended the CFE Treaty in 2007, and NATO stopped sharing information with Russia

[802] Within the framework of the NATO-Russia Council, practical military cooperation has been suspended, but there is a goal to maintain political dialogue

[803] The High North and the Arctic The Government considers the High North to be Norway's most important strategic area of ​​responsibility

[804] Norway has the right and obligation to ensure its own sovereignty and rights

[805] Norway has long placed emphasis on a presence in the northern sea areas to assert sovereignty, safeguard the exercise of authority, and contribute to predictability and stability

[806] This is an important part of the government's overall High North policy

[808] This applies to both territory located on the European mainland and islands such as Svalbard and Jan Mayen

[809] The High North as a region is still largely characterized by stability and cooperation

[810] It is in the interest of all Arctic states that this development continues

[811] Russia has legitimate interests in the north

[812] The Arctic and the highlands are of great importance to Russia, for military-strategic and also economic reasons

[813] Cooperation with Russia, based on international law, is a prerequisite for long-term stability in the region

[814] Although Russian strategies for the Arctic still emphasize international cooperation, it must be assumed that in given situations Russia will be able to consider military force as one of several relevant instruments in the North

[819] Norway's immediate vicinity will likely remain one of the most important patrol areas for Russian strategic submarines

[820] The region is also important for exercises, training and testing of new weapons systems

[821] The large investments in both materiel and training in recent times make Russia a much more capable military power in the north than it was just a few years ago

[822] Russian military activity in nearby Norwegian areas is not considered to be directed against Norway

[823] The purpose is primarily strategic deterrence as well as securing access to the North Atlantic for its capabilities on Kola

[824] The central role of these sea areas in the Russian bastion defense concept implies the possibility that Russia will deny or control access to sea and land areas that also include parts of Norwegian territory

[826] A possible activation of the concept could help prevent Allied reinforcements to Europe

[827] The Baltic Sea is a place where Russian and allied interests meet directly, and where Russia has acted more assertively

[828] Increased tension in the Baltic Sea region could trigger increased Russian military activity in the north and challenge the freedom of movement for allies in our immediate vicinity

[830] This constitutes a threat to international peace and security

[831] Economic challenges, youth unemployment, corruption, discriminatory policies, organized crime, and the rise of terrorist groups are destabilizing the regions

[833] Weak or no government control means that unrest and armed conflict can quickly spread across porous borders

[842] Violent conflicts and fragile states still characterize parts of Africa, partly due to a weak institutional and operational security architecture that is dependent on international support

[843] The UN and the African Union still play a crucial role in maintaining peace and stability in these areas

[844] The transnational challenges related to migration, violent extremism, and drug, arms and human trafficking are increasing and have consequences for European security

[845] While piracy in the western Indian Ocean has almost stopped, there has been a significant increase in pirate attacks in the Gulf of Guinea

[846] Extremist groups such as Al Shabaab and Boko Haram, several of them with ties to al-Qaeda or ISIL, also influence regional conflicts and constitute significant destabilizing factors

[847] Sexual violence is also used in several of the conflicts

[848] as a means of warfare

[851] Northeast Asia is moving towards becoming an economic and political center of gravity in the world

[852] At the same time, large parts of Southwest Asia are characterized by political and economic unrest

[853] Developments in Asia are generally characterized by strong economic growth and military buildup in general, as well as China's emergence as a central power with regional ambitions that lead to heightened rivalry between countries

[854] For now, the tension is of a regional nature, but conflicts of interest in the region have the potential to challenge global stability in the long term

[855] China's positioning in the region challenges American interests and the United States' central role in the region

[856] The US security guarantees to countries such as Japan and South Korea mean that the US is tying up a significant proportion of its military resources in the region

[857] This is an important reason for the increasing American attention to Asia

[858] The regime in North Korea appears highly unpredictable and challenges regional and global stability
