[1232] Commitment and continued restructuring

[1233] The government plans to make significant investments in the defense sector in the coming years

[1234] The transformation of the defense sector is an ongoing process that provides room for new opportunities and an enhanced ability to respond more quickly to changes and challenges in the environment

[1235] Restructuring involves developing competence to solve tasks in new ways, perfecting skills and adopting modern technology

[1236] Regardless of a significant financial commitment, there is a need for major changes in the Armed Forces that affect the organization, employees and local communities

[1237] The Government is proposing four main measures to direct the sector's resources towards strengthening the Armed Forces' operational capabilities

[1238] emergency preparedness, increased staffing and activity, investments in new prioritized capacities and continuous improvement and efficiency

[1239] The defense sector must be better able to carry out its tasks, including the most demanding ones

[1240] The first priority the government will give is to catch up on the backlog of emergency logistics and maintenance, in order to make the best possible use of the existing structure by increasing availability, reducing readiness times and thereby strengthening preparedness

[1241] To avoid new economic imbalances arising on the investment and operating side, the government has taken into account cost developments and a sustained higher operating level

[1242] The Government believes that it is necessary that a realistic understanding of the long-term cost picture be used as the basis for the sector's long-term planning, so as to ensure that investments can be applied and maintained over time

[1243] Increased staffing and activity

[1244] The government will increase the staffing of the operational part of the structure from

[1245] This will further strengthen operational capability

[1246] There will be an increased level of activity and increased military presence, especially in the highlands

[1247] Responsiveness, availability and endurance are strengthened and preparedness can thereby be increased from the current level of ambition

[1248] The readiness status will improve, which includes the ability to rapidly build up forces and receive allies, based on, among other things, further development of civil-military cooperation

[1249] These measures enable increased Norwegian participation in allied exercises and training, as well as contributions to international efforts

[1250] Increases in staffing and activity levels are being implemented despite a net reduction in the number of employees in the sector, because resources are being shifted from management and base operations to operational activities

[1251] Invest in new prioritized capacities

[1252] The renewal and modernization pace of the defense structure is necessary to maintain a relevant operational capability, and will be continued and further strengthened from 2019 onwards

[1253] The Government will acquire capabilities that support security and defense policy priorities

[1254] Experience shows that new, modern weapons systems have higher operating costs than the systems they replace

[1255] This is true despite the fact that they are often less personnel-intensive and that performance-based logistics is used to a greater extent, where the supplier is responsible for a large part of the after-supply and maintenance

[1256] Procurements must be assessed collectively based on operational effectiveness, long-term sustainability and implementation capability in the short and long term

[1257] It requires good and long-term planning

[1258] There is also a difficult contradiction here

[1259] While the threat landscape can change rapidly, changes to the Armed Forces' structure and acquisitions of new equipment are both costly and time-consuming

[1260] This must be taken into account when investing in new capacities

[1261] Continuous improvement and efficiency

[1262] During recent planning periods, the defense sector has freed up significant resources for higher-priority activities through base and structural measures and extensive improvement and efficiency work

[1263] Further development of this work is a key tool for achieving the goals in the government's long-term plan

[1264] Making the best possible use of community resources is an important part of corporate social responsibility

[1265] Strengthened efforts throughout the sector towards continuous improvement and efficiency are crucial to realizing a sustainable and cost-effective defense structure

[1266] The improvement and efficiency work is described in more detail in chapter

[1267] The Armed Forces in a societal perspective The Armed Forces, together with the rest of the defense sector, are a significant societal actor with businesses and activities across large parts of the country, and which affect many people

[1268] The armed forces are an integrated part of society and are in a mutual interaction with and dependence on their surroundings

[1269] The Armed Forces as a Social Actor A clear majority of the population supports the need for a strong and credible defense, and the will to defend has been solid over time

[1270] This support is expressed in several ways, including through the willingness of both sexes to complete their first-time service and through the Armed Forces' generally good reputation

[1271] The defense sector contributes to creating security for the state and society

[1272] For a functioning democracy, this is an important starting point for stability, democratic development and economic growth

[1273] Large parts of the activities of the Armed Forces and the defense sector benefit civil society, for example in the form of the assistance the Armed Forces provide upon request to civilian authorities in handling crises and disasters, but also in terms of jobs, production and dissemination of research, knowledge and analyses

[1274] The direct economic effect of the Armed Forces' presence and activity in the country is approximately NOK 30 billion, a level that has remained stable over several years

[1275] The military can impose burdens on the surrounding community in some cases

[1276] The activities of the armed forces require, among other things, access to large areas

[1277] Operations and training and exercise activities may cause noise and other external impacts on the environment

[1278] The Armed Forces must therefore be aware of these consequences for the environment, and constantly seek to reduce the burdensome footprint as much as possible

[1279] Contribution to value creation and jobs

[1280] The defense sector creates many jobs

[1281] The Armed Forces' host municipalities across the country should be recognized for their efforts in facilitating the Armed Forces' activities

[1282] The organization of the Armed Forces has been reduced in scope over the years, and the Armed Forces are therefore represented in fewer places than they were during the Cold War

[1283] In addition, a lower proportion of youth cohorts than previously are completing their first-time service

[1284] This means that fewer people now than before have a direct connection to the Armed Forces

[1285] It is therefore all the more important that the Armed Forces further develop contact with civil society and contribute to increased knowledge of and understanding of the role of the defense sector in society

[1286] The Armed Forces should be a visible, open and modern organization

[1287] This will help maintain a good recruitment base and ensure access to necessary expertise

[1288] The defense sector has a long tradition of taking on apprentices, and is Norway's largest apprenticeship company

[1289] Each year, the Armed Forces offer around 600 apprenticeships in about 30 different fields spread across the country

[1290] This provides unique opportunities to combine apprenticeship and first-time service

[1291] The apprenticeship scheme and its administration will be adapted to better meet the needs of the Armed Forces

[1292] The defense sector is experiencing increased collaboration with and flow of expertise to and from other sectors of society

[1293] For example, Forsvarsbygg offers a trainee scheme where new graduates in a number of fields can intern and get to know the business

[1294] The Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI) has established a scheme where they accept summer students from several different fields of study

[1295] The scheme attracts a high number of applicants from the major educational environments, and is an important recruitment arena for future employment at FFI

[1296] Industrial cooperation is an industrial policy instrument used by Norwegian authorities to secure and increase Norwegian industry's access to foreign defense-related markets, cf. Recommendation

[1297] S (2015–2016) to Report

[1298] St. 9 (2015–

[1299] By facilitating equal conditions of competition between different countries' defense industries, a foundation is laid that contributes to value creation, expertise and market opportunities for Norwegian industry

[1300] The defense sector contributes new technology and expertise through research and development, which is important for society's overall innovation and expertise development

[1301] The defense sector's expertise needs and production must be seen as part of society's overall resources

[1302] It is important to establish collaboration where appropriate, and ensure the flow of knowledge and expertise between the various organizations in the defense sector, and between the defense sector and the rest of society

[1303] Competence development and dissemination

[1304] The Armed Forces and FFI have long collaborated closely with civilian actors on the dissemination of information and knowledge

[1305] Based on the need to protect military installations and facilities, Forsvarsbygg has developed leading expertise in protection and security, including establishing a competence center for securing state property, buildings and facilities

[1306] The National Competence Center for Building Security will transfer experiences from the defense sector to other parts of the government sector, in addition to assisting owners and users of critical infrastructure in securing their assets and functions against terrorism, sabotage, espionage and other hostile attacks

[1307] The center collaborates with other key players in this area, including the National Security Authority (NSM), Statsbygg and the Police Security Service (PST

[1308] The government is investing in research and development of relevant technologies that the Armed Forces need, in collaboration between the Armed Forces, FFI and the defense industry

[1309] The Government emphasizes that the defense sector adapts and utilizes civilian-developed technology where this meets the needs of the Armed Forces

[1310] National operational needs shall be emphasized

[1311] FFI supports this development, in addition to supporting the utilization of new major military equipment that will be introduced in the coming years

[1312] FFI will place significant emphasis on proximity to the Armed Forces' operational and technological needs in research and collaboration

[1313] Defense technology can have major ripple effects and benefits for the civilian sector

[1314] The Government is considering opportunities for closer civil-military cooperation within research and technology development, nationally and internationally

[1315] Support for voluntary work The Ministry of Defence provides support to a number of voluntary organisations and other non-public actors that contribute to strengthening the population's knowledge and understanding of Norwegian defence and security policy, or that otherwise contribute to supporting the objectives and priorities of the Defence Forces

[1316] The government wants to continue supporting volunteer work, but too close ties should not develop between volunteering and government activities

[1317] The government's declaration on volunteerism from 2015 recognizes the voluntary sector as an independent and necessary actor in Norwegian society

[1318] The declaration defines a framework for the interaction between the state and the voluntary sector, and emphasizes that predictability and simplification should characterize the collaboration

[1319] The Declaration on Volunteering states that the government does not wish to regulate volunteering, but rather to support the uniqueness and driving force of volunteering by providing room for action, predictability, and facilitating growth from below

[1320] The Ministry of Defence shall use the overall objectives and principles set out in the voluntary declaration as guidelines for its grant management

[1321] Further development of total defense

[1322] The concept of total defense was developed in the aftermath of World War II

[1323] The basic principle of the traditional total defense concept was that society's total resources should be mobilized for the defense of the country, if necessary

[1324] The concept was tailored to meet an invasion threat

[1325] The Storting agreed to the recommendation

[1326] S. no. 234 (2003–2004), cf. St.prp

[1327] –2004) to an expansion and modernization of the total defense concept

[1328] The concept involves mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society in connection with prevention, emergency planning, crisis management and consequence management across the entire crisis spectrum, from peace via security policy crises to armed conflict

[1329] The total defense concept provides broad frameworks for civil-military cooperation

[1330] It provides the necessary flexibility in that civilian and military resources can be used to solve challenges to both societal and state security

[1331] The Armed Forces depend on society functioning as well as possible, even in times of crisis and armed conflict

[1332] Societal security therefore also significantly affects the Armed Forces' ability to safeguard national security

[1333] In times of extraordinary stress, civil society is in many cases dependent on support from the Armed Forces

[1334] Both considerations of good social economy and mutual dependence between civilian and military sides indicate that the total defense concept should be continued

[1335] However, there is a need to update some of the schemes in the concept to current conditions and future challenges

[1336] The Government will continuously adapt total defence so that society's overall resources can be utilized as effectively as possible, both for state and societal security

[1337] The Armed Forces' primary tasks and the ability to solve them must form the basis for the assistance tasks

[1338] The Armed Forces' support for civil society should nevertheless be more decisive for the organization and dimensioning of the Armed Forces' capacities in certain areas

[1339] The principle that the Armed Forces' assistance should be within the framework of available capacities at any given time will be continued

[1340] Civilian support for the Armed Forces has received little attention in recent years

[1341] At the same time, the Armed Forces' dependence on civilian deliveries has increased

[1342] Renewed emphasis must therefore be placed on civilian support for the Armed Forces

[1343] This is further highlighted by the fact that security policy developments increase the need for the Armed Forces to strengthen their preparedness

[1344] The Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Justice and Public Security have reviewed and assessed civil-military arrangements and mechanisms in total defence and adapted a number of older provisions to current conditions and future challenges, particularly in the upper part of the crisis spectrum

[1345] Total defense encompasses a wide range of actors within most sectors of society

[1346] To be able to cooperate in the best possible way, it is crucial that relevant actors in both the civilian and military sectors have good knowledge of current arrangements and mechanisms for civil-military cooperation within total defense

[1347] In April 2015, the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Justice and Public Security published a revised edition of the publication Support and Cooperation, which provides a description of total defence

[1348] The purpose of the encyclopedia is to help anchor the current total defense concept in the civilian and military sectors

[1349] At the same time, the description of current arrangements and mechanisms will form an important part of the basis for further developing total defense

[1350] The Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI) has carried out projects in the series since

[1351] Protection of the community (BAS

[1352] In the BAS projects, FFI works closely with both civilian authorities and the defense sector

[1353] The BAS 8 project "Civil-military crisis management and preparedness" will run until 2018, and aims to contribute to improving civil-military cooperation within the framework of total defense, to develop methods for understanding risk and vulnerability, and to utilize crosssectoral crisis exercises

[1354] As an integrated part of BAS 8, FFI will complete a research assignment entitled "Civilian support to the Armed Forces in security policy crises and war

[1355] Furthermore, the project will investigate the need for civil protection measures

[1356] The Armed Forces' need for support from civil society

[1357] In a serious crisis situation and in armed conflict, the Armed Forces' need for civilian support in the form of services, goods, personnel and access to infrastructure will exceed the resources the Armed Forces need on a daily basis

[1358] Key needs for the Armed Forces will be road, rail, sea and air transport (with associated infrastructure) for the movement of personnel, materiel and supplies, as well as evacuation

[1359] Furthermore, access to civilian health personnel and civilian health services, and more specialized services such as maintenance and engineering services, is critical

[1360] There will be a need for supplies of a number of goods, with fuel supplies to support transport services and Armed Forces operations being among the most important

[1361] Both civilian suppliers that support the Armed Forces, and to some extent the Armed Forces themselves, are also dependent on basic services such as power supply and, increasingly, civilian ICT infrastructure and services

[1362] Reduced readiness times for military units also mean that support must be able to be in place more quickly

[1363] Development of emergency plans and emergency response bodies

[1364] The Norwegian Armed Forces are in the process of finalizing extensive work to revise and update emergency preparedness plans and operational plans

[1365] These plans assume that the entire national force structure and allied reinforcements must be able to be supported simultaneously

[1366] Based on these plans, national needs and the need for support for possible bilateral military reinforcements can be determined with a reasonable degree of accuracy

[1367] Regarding other allied reinforcements, due to NATO's reinforcement planning, there will be a need for some flexibility in planning

[1368] The Armed Forces will also prepare requirements assessments based on the most likely alternatives

[1369] In addition to being able to meet known and quantifiable needs for civilian support, the civilian side must, as far as possible, also be able to support the unforeseen needs of military forces

[1370] Civilian support for the Armed Forces must be included to a greater extent in the work on national emergency preparedness plans in the civilian sector

[1371] The Armed Forces' logistics needs are covered, among other things, through the Armed Forces' own resources, other public resources, commercial agreements, cooperation with the business community and requisitioning

[1372] The needs of the Armed Forces shall be based to the greatest extent possible on commercial agreements, if necessary with contingency clauses where this is cost-effective

[1373] The Armed Forces can also requisition necessary goods, services and infrastructure pursuant to the Requisition Act

[1374] However, small inventories mean that requisitioning is in many cases an unsuitable tool for some consumer goods

[1375] Requisition is more suitable for materials, services and infrastructure

[1376] In an emergency situation, the needs of the Armed Forces must be given high priority

[1377] However, this must be balanced against critical needs in civil society

[1378] A modern society depends on a number of capacities in order to function

[1379] Both when preparing plans and during exercises, it must be clarified what capacities civil society must have in order to function, and the consequences of civil society providing capacity to the Armed Forces

[1380] The Ministry of Defense will also be able to approach other ministries to gain access to resources

[1381] In such cases, the ministries' authority to issue regulations based on the Emergency Preparedness Act or to use emergency preparedness provisions in their own sectoral regulations will be relevant instruments

[1382] The Ministry of Defence has initiated a dialogue with relevant ministries to identify appropriate instruments

[1383] This primarily affects the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, the Ministry of Health and Care Services, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries, the Ministry of Transport and Communications, and the Ministry of Petroleum and Energy

[1384] In situations where it is not possible to obtain sufficient resources, it becomes necessary to prioritize between civilian and military needs

[1385] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security will, by virtue of its coordination responsibility, assess whether existing prioritization mechanisms are sufficient

[1386] Regardless of how the resources are obtained, the Armed Forces will pay for the relevant goods and services and the use of infrastructure in line with the sector principle

[1387] However, with advance requisitioning, most of the costs will only be incurred when the resources are actually put to use

[1388] This avoids tying up funds that could be used for the more focused aspects of the Armed Forces' activities, which is good economics

[1389] If the specific needs of the Armed Forces require measures on the civilian side that have cost-related consequences, this shall be covered by the Armed Forces, unless otherwise stated in law, regulations or a special agreement

[1390] Cooperation and emergency response bodies under the various ministries must be adapted to the necessary extent to challenges in connection with security policy crises and armed conflict in order to be able to meet both known and unforeseen needs

[1391] In this context, both civilian and military representation in emergency response bodies should also be considered to contribute to regular information exchange between the civilian and military sectors

[1392] The Armed Forces will, especially in times of crisis and armed conflict, be dependent on services provided by civilian personnel in the Armed Forces, in the public sector in general, and in business and industry

[1393] This has international law implications, and a clear boundary is required for the use of civilian personnel in armed conflict

[1394] The defense sector must at all times ensure that planning for and implementation of civilian support to the Armed Forces is in accordance with international law

[1395] Practice and training

[1396] Exercises are crucial for strengthening cooperation between the civilian and military sectors

[1397] Exercises help build competence

[1398] In addition, weaknesses identified during exercises will be used in the work to improve and coordinate emergency preparedness plans

[1399] In addition, it can be expected that trained emergency response agencies will have a shorter reaction time

[1400] It is therefore necessary that civilian support for the Armed Forces becomes a greater integrated part of the exercise activities, and that this is included in both civilian and military exercise programs

[1401] This applies to everything from simple staff exercises to larger cross-sectoral staff and field exercises

[1402] A strengthened capability and preparedness for civilian support to the Armed Forces will also strengthen society's ability to handle challenges to societal security, and is therefore an important contribution to comprehensive preparedness

[1403] The Armed Forces are the only actor in society that can be responsible for the military defense of the country

[1404] It must be ensured that military operational capacities are not tied to civil preparedness in a way that reduces the ability to carry out military tasks, unless otherwise decided

[1405] In the event of simultaneous crises of a civil and military nature, the Armed Forces' resources will be prioritized to solve the military tasks

[1406] For the military operational capacities on which civil preparedness is entirely dependent, special agreements and arrangements shall apply

[1407] The Armed Forces have a long tradition of supporting civil society

[1408] This is correct from a socio-economic perspective, because the Armed Forces possess resources that naturally benefit civilian society when the situation requires it

[1409] Collaboration across sectors in society is appropriate to avoid unnecessary duplication of capacities and to improve preparedness in society

[1410] The Armed Forces' support for civilian authorities is broad-based

[1411] Firstly, the Armed Forces carry out civilian tasks as part of their ongoing, daily operations

[1412] Important examples are the Coast Guard's supervisory authority within fishing and trapping, environmental protection and customs, the Border Guard's border surveillance, His Majesty the King's Guard's guarding of the Royal House and contribution to preparedness in the capital area, and the Intelligence Service's production of intelligence for national authorities

[1413] Secondly, upon request, the Armed Forces assist the police and other civilian authorities to safeguard public safety when civilian resources are insufficient, for example in the event of natural disasters, accidents and serious criminal acts such as terrorism

[1414] The police and other civil authorities are responsible for handling such incidents, and the Armed Forces are therefore in a supporting role

[1415] The Armed Forces also collaborate with civilian authorities throughout the entire societal security chain, from knowledge and overview of risk and vulnerability, through prevention, preparedness, crisis management and reconstruction to learning

[1416] Basically, the main elements of the Armed Forces' structure are dimensioned to solve the Armed Forces' task

[1417] At the same time, support for civil society must be included in the assessment of the organization and dimensioning of certain capacities in the Armed Forces

[1418] This is relevant, among other things, when designing dedicated missions, emergency preparedness orders, localization, requirements for training, exercises and practice, and the ability to collaborate with actors outside the defense sector

[1419] Although the Armed Forces' structure and operational capabilities are primarily developed to solve military tasks, some capabilities are also relevant to and therefore geared towards assisting civilian authorities

[1420] The Armed Forces' special forces and the Armed Forces' helicopter capacity have dedicated missions and preparedness, which means that the police's need for assistance is partly decisive for the organization, equipment, staffing and training of these capacities

[1421] This also applies to some extent to the Home Guard

[1422] Other selected units are also on crisis and aid readiness

[1423] This entails requirements for adapted operational capability and response time to quickly resolve more specifically specified tasks related to crisis management and assistance to civil authorities

[1424] Further development of the Armed Forces' assistance and support

[1425] In recent years, further developing the Armed Forces' assistance to civilian authorities has been a priority

[1426] Improvement measures have been implemented for, among other things, the Home Guard, the special forces and helicopter readiness

[1427] Regulations and procedures have been improved

[1428] Planning has become better coordinated between the civilian and military sectors

[1429] It has been a priority to conduct more targeted exercises to increase the ability of civilian and military actors to operate together

[1430] The dialogue between civilian and military actors has been strengthened

[1431] The cooperation between the Police Security Service and the Intelligence Service has been strengthened through the establishment of the Joint Counterterrorism Center (FKTS

[1432] The Government will continue to further develop the defense sector's ability to assist civilian authorities in maintaining public security

[1433] The Armed Forces' own needs will still be most important for developing the Armed Forces' structure and capabilities

[1434] The Armed Forces' support for civil society should nevertheless be a greater determinant of the organization and dimensioning of the Armed Forces' capacities within the areas of maritime counterterrorism and infection control transport

[1435] Furthermore, further assessments will be made of how and to what extent this will also apply within the areas

[1436] Bomb preparedness and explosives disposal, CBRNE preparedness, transport, rescue services, reconnaissance and surveillance, engineering support, ICT support, NIS services (Intelligence Service, Police Security Service, National Security Authority and Defence Security Department) and handling threats in the digital space

[1437] As a general principle, in the case of major investments in the Armed Forces that may also have beneficial value for civilian authorities, relevant civilian authorities should be contacted to clarify whether there are assistance and support needs and opportunities for multiple use, and these should be included in the assessment

[1438] Utility value in the context of development assistance should also be emphasized in the case of smaller investments in the Armed Forces

[1439] The Armed Forces' support to civilian authorities is financed in accordance with the sectoral responsibility principle, where the authority that benefits from any new capacities, missions and emergency preparedness requirements ensures the financing of this

[1440] For cost coverage of assistance, there are no plans to change the current provision that the Armed Forces cover their own additional costs in the emergency phase

[1441] Within the framework of current regulations and principles for civil-military cooperation, all available resources of the Armed Forces shall initially be made available, depending on the needs of civilian authorities in a crisis situation

[1442] When the Armed Forces make equipment available to the police, and special expertise is required to use the equipment, the Armed Forces must also contribute to this

[1443] A main priority in this long-term plan is to strengthen the Armed Forces' operational capability

[1444] This can also provide a better ability to assist in civil crisis management, and thus improve society's overall preparedness

[1445] For example, many of the Armed Forces' capacities for handling traditional armed attacks will also be relevant in the event of terrorist attacks

[1446] The Government continues the principle that, as a general rule, new military capabilities or structures should not be acquired specifically to provide support to civil society

[1447] Further development of special capacities and areas The ability of special forces to support civil society in national crisis management, including counterterrorism, has been strengthened in recent years

[1448] Both the Armed Forces Special Command and the Marine Hunter Command are now on national counter-terrorism alert to assist the police

[1449] To continue the development of support for civil society, the special forces must be ensured sufficient and relevant exercises and training in aid scenarios

[1450] The Norwegian Armed Forces' helicopter readiness to support the police has been gradually strengthened after the terrorist attacks on 22 July 2011, and Bell helicopters are now on one-hour standby for both general and enforcement assistance to the police

[1451] The Armed Forces' other helicopter resources can also be used if necessary

[1452] The armed forces' transport aircraft are a relevant resource, but the maritime patrol aircraft, submarines and fighter jets also have capabilities that can support special forces in counter-terrorism operations. The Home Guard is, through its presence and local knowledge, an important resource for supporting civil society

[1453] The Home Guard has been strengthened in recent years with more training and better equipment, which also provides an improved ability to assist civilian authorities

[1454] Although the Home Guard is dimensioned according to its military tasks, it is also important to further develop the ability to cooperate with civilian authorities

[1455] The Home Guard can assist both in the event of accidents and natural disasters and in terrorist preparedness

[1456] The Home Guard is a particularly relevant assistance resource for police object security

[1457] The Home Guard's structure and tasks related to object security have been clarified after the terrorist attacks on July

[1458] Instructions for securing objects with security forces from 2012 provide clear guidelines for close cooperation between the police and the Armed Forces

[1459] The two agencies will work together to ensure that plans for securing all objects reported from the police to the Armed Forces are completed in 2016, and that securing the objects is practiced within the available resource framework

[1460] What really matters is a study on more efficient organization of reinforcement resources for the Home Guard, Civil Defense and Police Reserve

[1461] A working group with representatives from the Armed Forces and a number of civilian emergency response actors has, based on the study, submitted a report with proposals for specific follow-up measures

[1462] The report, together with NOU 2013, will form the basis for the Ministry of Justice and Public Security and the Ministry of Defence's work to further develop the cooperation between the three actors

[1463] Intelligence Service** The Intelligence Service supports both civilian and military authorities in providing a necessary basis for decision-making in matters concerning foreign, security and defense policy

[1464] The intelligence service's important contribution to civilian authorities is increasing, and includes, among other things, the collection of information on international terrorism and on the production and proliferation of weapons of mass destruction

[1465] The Intelligence Service cooperates with the Police Security Service on security threats within the framework of a separate instruction and the overall legal basis for the services

[1466] The Joint Counterterrorism Center was established in 2013, and is staffed with personnel from both the Police Security Service and the Intelligence Service

[1467] The further development of the cooperation between the two services will continue in the period 2017–2020, including by further strengthening cooperation on tasks related to threats in the digital space

[1468] This also includes strengthening the cooperation the two services have with NSM

[1469] The three services have collaborated for several years, including through the Cyber Coordination Group, which meets regularly

[1470] It is being considered to further develop cooperation within the group by co-locating resources

[1471] In this way, even closer cooperation is facilitated in the daily work of addressing digital threats

[1472] Assistance in the event of unwanted ICT incidents** The Armed Forces' resources are designed and dimensioned based on the responsibility for securing the defense sector's own systems

[1473] Relevant scenarios for digital attacks show an increasing degree of targeted attacks against individual sectors

[1474] A model for incident management where personnel with relevant expertise assist the vulnerable sector will be considered

[1475] In special cases, the Armed Forces can also be used to establish or re-establish communications infrastructure, including classified ICT systems

[1476] The Armed Forces' relevant resources available at any given time should be included in such a model

[1477] In a situation with a risk of extensive digital attacks against critical infrastructure, the defense sector's resources will primarily have to be prioritized to ensure the security of its own ICT systems

[1478] As with other types of crises and incidents, in the case of ICT incidents it may also be appropriate for the Armed Forces to support with general resources such as emergency power, security and security, transport and handling of consequential damage

[1479] CBRNE preparedness** The Armed Forces have a limited capacity to handle incidents involving CBRNE agents (chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive agents

Medical air evacuation and medical emergency teams The Armed Forces have the capacity for medical air transport, both through their own aircraft and an agreement with a civil airline, which can be made available to civil authorities

[1495] To the extent that the Armed Forces have other relevant special equipment (for example for night search), this can also be made available

[2016] The Home Guard 5.5.1 General information on missions and development

[2017] The Home Guard has a nationwide territorial responsibility that involves guarding and securing important objects and infrastructure, territorial surveillance and control, facilitating and receiving allied reinforcements, and civil-military cooperation

[2018] The Home Guard has an important role in establishing local situational awareness and in receiving allied forces

[2019] The Home Guard does not operate outside Norway's borders, but HV personnel participate in international operations as part of other branches of defense's force contributions

[2020] Operational ambition

[2021] The Home Guard must be able to establish presence, situational awareness and protection of military infrastructure and local populations in vulnerable areas in the event of security crises and further escalation of the situation

[2022] The Home Guard will quickly provide well-trained and practiced personnel to guard and secure the highest priority military and civilian objects

[2023] In addition, at the request of the responsible authority, the Home Guard shall provide available resources to support civil society in the event of accidents, natural disasters, and terrorist incidents

[2024] The Home Guard shall assume territorial responsibility on behalf of the Commander of the Home Guard through civil-military cooperation with other societal actors, and contribute with force protection when receiving and moving allied reinforcements arriving in Norway

[2025] The Home Guard's task forces should be able to be deployed in a flexible manner throughout the country where the need is greatest

[2026] Home Guard leadership The Home Guard Commander will have overall responsibility as a force commander located in Terningmoen

[2027] A national territorial command element (National Territorial Command, NTK) is established for tactical command of the Home Guard forces

[2028] This strengthens the ability to lead and coordinate the Home Guard's tasks and operations throughout the country, for example during allied reception and when transferring forces between districts

[2029] The district staffs in Troms and Finnmark are being strengthened by providing them with additional personnel

[2030] This increases the ability to manage Home Guard forces, coordinate with civil authorities, and receive allies in important geographical areas

[2031] In order to carry out the necessary strengthening of priority areas and to adapt the number of staff to a somewhat smaller structure, the government recommends disbanding the district staff HV

[2032] There will still be local HV forces to carry out tasks in the areas, but under the leadership of other district headquarters

[2033] Contact with local authorities and regional expertise are handled by responsible district staff

[2034] The Home Guard's force structure

[2035] The reduction of the Home Guard's task force from 5,000 to 3,000 has been completed in the current four-year period, and the new task force structure has been well implemented

[2036] The goal of an area structure of 42,000 personnel has not been achieved

[2037] It is particularly challenging to fill the structure in Finnmark, which is due to a low recruitment base

[2038] In order to adapt the area structure to the real situation, the government recommends a reduction from the current plan number of 42,000 personnel to 35,000 personnel

[2039] The reduction contributes to a focus on prioritized capacities

[2040] The need for guarding and securing military infrastructure has been somewhat reduced, partly due to changes resulting from new communications technology

[2041] The crews in the Home Guard's task forces have a high level of responsiveness and a better level of training and equipment than the departments in the regional structure

[2042] Experience has shown that there is great motivation for service in the task forces

[2043] The task forces will therefore continue at the current level of 3,000 personnel

[2044] Arrangements must be made to ensure that the task forces can be used flexibly throughout the country where the need is greatest

[2045] This maintains the ability to respond quickly to military missions, reinforce the regional structure, handle missions beyond what the regional structure has capacity for, or support civilian crisis management

[2046] The tasks of the Norwegian Maritime Home Guard (SHV) are force protection, contribution to the protection of objects with a sea front and establishment of local situational awareness along the coast

[2047] The Norwegian Maritime Home Guard command structure has been closed down and the SHV departments are now organizationally part of the HV districts, where nine out of eleven HV districts have SHV departments

[2054] The Armed Forces' Special Forces

[2055] General information about assignments and development

[2056] The special forces are a strategic capacity that conducts operations across the entire conflict scale from peace to crisis and armed conflict to achieve national strategic or operational objectives

[2057] The forces can be used in the full spectrum of military special operations. In January 2014, the special forces were organized under a separate operational unit in the Armed Forces and given the name Norwegian Armed Forces Special Forces

[2058] The Armed Forces Special Command is located in Rena Camp and the Marine Hunter Commando is located at Haakonsvern Naval Station

[2059] The Norwegian Armed Forces Special Forces Command and the Norwegian Marine Fighter Command were transferred from the Army and the Navy respectively and subordinated to the Norwegian Armed Forces Special Forces

[2060] The main purpose of establishing the Armed Forces' Special Forces was to improve management, development and use to ensure a relevant operational capability

[2061] In line with societal developments, special forces have increasingly been designed to contribute to problem solving across the entire spectrum of conflicts

[2062] The special forces are a relevant resource with high availability, and in recent years have participated in several international operations while maintaining national preparedness

[2063] Cooperation with the police has been further strengthened during this period

[2064] This strengthens Norway's ability to manage crises

[2065] Against the backdrop of increasing complexity within special operations, due to technological development and a changing threat landscape, special forces will be further developed

[2066] Beyond military special operations, this applies to support for counterterrorism, crisis management and hostage rescue

[2067] These are tasks that require high responsiveness and broad support from other parts of the Armed Forces

[2068] The most important measure is to dedicate

[2069] Bell 412 helicopters as helicopter capability in support of the special forces

[2070] Operational ambition

[2071] The special forces are a strategic capacity that should be able to carry out operations within the entire conflict scale from peace to crisis and armed conflict

[2072] The main tasks of the special forces will continue as they are today

[2073] The special forces must be able to carry out the full range of special operations in all domains, independently or within an allied framework

[2074] The force's unique capabilities can be used both before, during and after a national joint operational operation as part of the national defense

[2075] The Norwegian Armed Forces' special forces must at all times be able to provide forces for international crisis management as an independent contribution or as part of an allied framework

[2076] Furthermore, the special forces contribute flexible and unique capabilities that can be used independently or as support to other authorities, including the Ministry of Justice and Public Security and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

[2077] The special forces will provide forces for continuous national crisis management preparedness, including counterterrorism preparedness in support of the police, as well as hostage rescue abroad

[2078] The special forces must have the ability to cooperate across sectors in all types of crises and conflicts that may arise both nationally and internationally

[2260] The defense sector's base and support structure must be modernized and streamlined so that a larger portion of the sector's resources can be used for operational activities

[2261] The base and support structure has not been modernized in line with the restructuring of the operational structure and is therefore still very extensive

[2262] The Norwegian Armed Forces manage approximately four million square meters of buildings with over 12,000 buildings and facilities spread over 700 locations in the country

[2263] The defense sector spends a disproportionate amount of resources on operating buildings and facilities

[2264] The Government will therefore make a much-needed reduction in the number of bases, streamline management and continue the modernization of logistics

[2265] The measures will contribute to a long-term balance between the Armed Forces' operational structure, force production, bases and support activities

[2266] The Armed Forces' base structure shall support the Armed Forces' ability to carry out its tasks throughout the country

[2267] The base structure does not have a direct operational value, but it can be a prerequisite for successful operations in peace, crisis and armed conflict, for both national and allied forces

[2268] In peacetime, the bases are used for force production, exercises and training of our own and allied forces

[2269] The national and allied activity and presence in nearby Norwegian areas contributes to stability

[2270] Access to necessary bases and facilities for military activity provides an opportunity for rapid deployment and reception of allied forces in crisis and armed conflict

[2271] The long-term development of the base structure must therefore, in addition to the daily need for force production, facilitate national and allied defense plans

[2272] However, it is important to emphasize that the base structure itself provides neither operational capability nor defensive capability

[2273] For this reason, the closure of bases such as Kjevik, Kjeller, Setnesmoen or the bases being closed in the Harstad area does not mean that the affected regions will be less well defended in a possible conflict

[2274] Today's base structure is a legacy from a time when the Armed Forces had a significantly larger structure

[2275] A relevant and modern defense structure that will meet the future threat situation with modern sensor systems and long-range weapons requires a different approach, and the ability and willingness to develop

[2276] The government prioritizes increased activity in the north and therefore recommends a strengthened base for air operations in the north, a strengthening of the Border Guard and a continued focus on Ramsund as a maritime logistics base for both surface vessels and submarines

[2277] In addition, the Coast Guard base at Sortland will continue

[2278] Furthermore, the government prioritizes increased protection of the bases

[2279] The armed forces' base and support structure is vulnerable and demanding to protect

[2280] Bases that are to function as combat bases in a situation where modern sensor systems and long-range weapons are used must have sufficient protection and be built in a way that limits damage from possible attacks and impacts

[2281] The Armed Forces' base and support structure must be as suitable as possible for its own operations, force production and allied presence, exercises and training in peacetime

[2282] At the same time, the structure must also be suitable for receiving allies and supporting operations in crisis and armed conflict, in combination with the utilization of civilian airports and port facilities

[2283] The combat base at Evenes is an example of such a facility

[2284] Plans for national and allied utilization of both military base structures and civilian infrastructure in crisis and armed conflict will be updated

[2286] The Government will introduce the principle that best practices for the various building categories will be used as the basis for future EBA investments and for the management of the property portfolio

[2287] The government will therefore introduce cost-reducing measures and incentives for both investments and operations

[2288] The sector should be based on standardized, sober solutions, where access to local adaptations should be limited

[2301] S (2014–2015) informed about the status regarding the costs of establishing the fighter air base on Ørland

[2303] In the proposal, the Ministry of Defence pointed to two areas where there remained a significant risk that costs would be higher than assumed in the proposal

[2304] S (2011–

[2305] Firstly, the interpretation of the regulations for measures and acquisition of noise exposed properties is stricter than that which was based on the strategic impact assessment

[2306] In August 2015, the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation confirmed the municipality's zoning plan decision from November 2014 regarding limit values for indoor and outdoor noise in existing buildings

[2307] The decision entails a significant increase in the costs associated with the offer to purchase buildings and the implementation of noise measures on both municipal and private buildings around the combat air base compared to the assumptions

[2308] Updated calculations show an estimated cost increase of approximately NOK 850 million

[2309] The other factor that has contributed to increasing costs is protection and security measures at the base

[2310] Increased demands are now being placed on the protection and security of the base and on the hangar solution for the F

[2311] Studies conducted by the Norwegian Defence Research Institute show that a combination of effective air defense and a spread of hangars for the new combat aircraft will reduce vulnerability more than a centralized hangar solution that is heavily fortified

[2312] The chosen solution will also facilitate efficient flight hour production

[2313] In addition, significantly less of the existing infrastructure at Ørland is being reused than was initially planned in 2011, partly because the base is in full operational operation with F-16s, while at the same time being expanded for the new F-35 fighter jets

[2314] Overall, these conditions result in approximately NOK 750 million in additional costs for the hangar solution at the fighter base

[2315] In total, the stricter noise requirements, security measures and hangar solutions result in an additional need of approximately NOK 1.6 billion for the establishment of the fighter air base on Ørland

[2328] As part of the basis for the government's recommendation, the following alternative solutions have been considered

[2329] Summary of the activity at Evenes – decommissioning of Andøya air station

[2330] Collection of activity on Andøya – decommissioning of Evenes air station

[2331] Sharing the activity between Evenes and Andøya

[2332] Collection of activities at Evenes – continuation of Andøya as a contingency base

[2333] Collection of activities on Andøya – continuation of Evenes as a contingency base

[2334] In addition, a socio-economic analysis has been carried out, which is discussed in more detail under section

[2335] Government recommendation – collection of activity at Evenes (alternative

[2336] The collection of fighter aircraft and maritime patrol aircraft at Evenes, protected by long-range air defense and base defense, provides a compact and effective solution that provides good protection for the Air Force's resources

[2337] In addition, Evenes is an area that is important for receiving allied forces

[2338] A collection of resources at Evenes, protected by long-range air defense, is therefore the best solution operationally

[2339] Evenes, with its modest and scattered buildings, is also better equipped to deal with noise challenges than is the case on Andøya

[2340] Noise conditions were a decisive factor in the choice of Evenes over Andøya as a forward combat air base in the previous long-term plan

[2341] Evenes is the most recently established of the Norwegian Armed Forces' air stations, and much of the existing buildings and facilities can therefore be reused

[2342] This particularly applies to the necessary facilities for fighter aircraft, air defense and base defense

[2343] A base at Evenes also has personnel advantages

[2344] The proximity to Harstad and Narvik provides opportunities for jobs and education for employees' families who will settle in the area

[2345] The government's proposal to consolidate the activity at Evenes involves an increase of about 600 employees and over 300 conscripts at Evenes

[2346] Due to smaller personnel and economies of scale for the support functions on the ground, this option has operating costs that are approximately NOK 200 million lower per year from 2027 compared to a shared solution

[2347] The proposed concentration of activity at Evenes will require investments in administrative buildings, accommodation and housing

[2348] In addition, there is a need for investments in flight operational facilities, about NOK 700 million for security measures and about NOK 150 million for noise-related measures

[2349] Necessary security measures include external and internal perimeter security, surveillance systems, and mail and goods reception

[2350] The assessment of security measures is based on new legislation and regulations as well as experiences from the establishment of the fighter air base on Ørland

[2351] The need for noise-related investments has increased compared to the calculations based on Prop

[2352] –2012), due to a stricter interpretation of the regulations for requirements for measures

[2353] A total investment requirement of approximately NOK 3.5 billion has been calculated for the collection of activity at Evenes

[2354] Collection of activity on Andøya (alternative

[2355] The collection of fighter aircraft and maritime patrol aircraft on Andøya, protected by long-range air defense, also provides a compact and effective solution with satisfactory protection

[2356] Andøya's location makes the base somewhat more challenging to protect than Evenes

[2357] The reception area in Ofoten will also not be protected in the same way as at a gathering in Evenes

[2358] Andøya is well placed for a large degree of reuse of facilities, especially for the flight operations environments

[2359] The need for approximately doubling the number of employees and conscripts entails investments in administrative buildings, barracks and housing

[2360] In addition, there are investments in flight operational facilities

[2361] Fighter aircraft operations from Andøya will cause a significant increase in noise at Andenes

[2362] Several solutions have been considered here

[2363] The solution that provides both the least noise consequences and the lowest costs is to extend the crosswind path to conduct as many combat aircraft operations as possible there

[2364] Fighter aircraft are more sensitive to wind than maritime patrol aircraft, so use of both runways must be considered to achieve similar regularity as for Evenes

[2365] This means that, combined with the development of the crosswind path at approximately three billion kroner, redemption and noise measures on buildings are expected to cost over two billion kroner

[2366] This is based on new noise calculations from Sintef which also take into account the experiences from Ørland

[2367] In addition, security measures worth approximately NOK 720 million must be implemented at the base if both combat aircraft and maritime patrol aircraft are to be stationed here

[2368] An investment requirement of approximately NOK 8.7 billion has been calculated for a concentration of activity on Andøya

[2369] Sharing the activity between Andøya and Evenes (alternative

[2370] For the study of this alternative, it is assumed that only the base that has combat aircraft will be protected by air defense

[2371] If both bases were to receive such protection, the costs associated with investments and especially operations would increase significantly

[2372] The fighter jets are expected to be located in Evenes as agreed, and the maritime patrol aircraft will be located on Andøya

[2373] The solution provides the same protection for the reception area in Ofoten, but the maritime patrol aircraft will not come under the protection of the air defense at Evenes

[2374] This means that these resources will have to deploy to another base at a given threat level

[2375] The alternative entails two base and support structures, thus eliminating the economies of scale that a collection on one base provides

[2376] The solution also entails costs for securing two bases

[2377] A less protected base for the maritime patrol aircraft means that investment is made in a base that will have limited use in crisis and armed conflict

[2378] As with the other alternatives, extensive reuse of buildings and facilities is also assumed here, but due to operation on two bases, this solution requires more employees and conscripts with the associated need for investments in administrative buildings, barracks, and housing

[2379] A total investment requirement of approximately NOK 3.5 billion has been estimated

[2380] Due to more personnel and overlap of a number of support functions and material needs, this alternative has significantly higher operating costs, over 200 million kroner more per year, compared to a collection at Evenes

[2381] Accumulated over 20 years, this cost difference amounts to over NOK 4 billion

[2382] Continuation as emergency bases (alternatives 4 and

[2383] The two options, where the base that is closed down as an air station is continued as a contingency base, combine the advantages of gathering and air defense protection of national resources at one base with a more robust base structure in the north

[2384] Retaining a base as a contingency base means that the Armed Forces continue to provide the necessary infrastructure for their own and/or allied operations in crisis and armed conflict, without Norwegian units being stationed there in peacetime

[2385] However, operation and maintenance of this infrastructure results in significant additional costs through minimum requirements for airport operations and runway conditions, along with a need to retain large parts of the base in order to maintain the possibility of combat aircraft operations

[2386] The runway system must be maintained in its full length, and fuel and aircraft parking capacity must be maintained

[2387] In addition, ammunition stocks must be maintained

[2388] Airport operations, including tower services, fire, rescue and accident services, can be transferred to a civilian operator for the alternative of Andøya as a contingency base, but it must be assumed that the Armed Forces must cover part of the costs of such cooperation

[2389] Alternative 4, with a consolidation of the activity at Evenes and a continuation of Andøya as a contingency base, appears to be the only real alternative of the two

[2390] Alternative 5 requires even greater investments than collection on Andøya

[2391] Assuming a sharing of costs with Avinor for airport operations, additional costs of approximately NOK 100 million per year are still expected compared to if Andoya airport is closed

[2392] In addition, reinvestments will be incurred over time

[2393] Continuing Andøya as a contingency base for 20 years will, including reinvestments, cost about NOK 2.7 billion more than a closure combined with the collection of resources at Evenes

[2394] The costs of Evenes as a contingency base are lower due to significantly more extensive civilian air traffic and an airport that is civilian run

[2487] Consolidation and streamlining of the Norwegian Armed Forces Personnel and Conscription Center

[2488] In the period 2017–2020, the government will consolidate and streamline the activities of the Norwegian Armed Forces Personnel and Conscription Centre (FPVS) and shift the centre of gravity northwards

[2489] As of August 1, 2016, FPVS will be located with branches in Oslo, Hamar, Elverum and Harstad, as well as with local session centers in Bergen, Kristiansand, Målselv, Stavanger, Trondheim and Oslo

[2490] In addition, the Armed Forces' narcotics groups north and south are subordinate to the FPVS

[2493] Modernization and development of the support structure in the defense sector

[2494] The Government will carry out a comprehensive modernization of the support structure in the Armed Forces, including the logistics area

[2495] Supply and maintenance can be based to a much greater extent on deliveries from the civilian market

[2496] The use of strategic agreements with civilian suppliers provides benefits such as efficient use of time and resources, increased responsiveness and flexibility, greater operational room for maneuver, improved endurance and increased operational availability

[2497] This development within civil-military cooperation gives the Armed Forces room to reduce their own organization

[2498] At the same time, it is essential that performance is adapted to a much greater extent to real needs, and that agreements must be made that ensure sufficient logistics deliveries even in times of crisis and armed conflict

[2499] Organization of logistics activities The need for modernization and development of logistics activities combined with an extensive and complex portfolio of investments in the defense sector in the coming years means that the Armed Forces are in the process of implementing measures related to the organization and capacity of logistics activities in the sector

[2500] The Norwegian Defence Logistics Organisation (FLO

[2501] FLO is organized under the Chief of Defence, and is continued with an additional professionalized staff with responsibility for supply, maintenance, transport and operational logistics units that cannot naturally be placed under the branches of defence, including the National Logistics Command (NLK

[2502] These services will form the basis for the further development of logistics activities in the Armed Forces

[2503] Supply, which includes operational procurement, storage and distribution of materiel and spare parts, will continue, but will be streamlined based on increased civil-military cooperation

[2504] This is a process The Armed Forces

[2505] Everything has begun according to the principle that civilian suppliers are only used where this is most cost-effective

[2506] A new common management system for all equipment has been introduced through the LOS program

[2507] With the exception of Karljohansvern, the heavy workshops will continue in FLO until further notice, but during this period, strategic collaboration with the defense industry will be considered to streamline maintenance activities

[2508] In order to bring together small professional communities, exploit synergies and raise professional quality, the government will organizationally transfer the following departments belonging to the Norwegian Defence Centre for Logistics and Operational Support (FKL) from the Army to FLO; FKL staff, including the logistics department, technical department, the Logistics School, the Norwegian Defence Ammunition and EOD School, the Norwegian Defence Transport School and operational support

[2509] The Army retains the Logistics Base Land, the Armed Forces Competence Center for Object Security, the Armed Forces Dog Training School and the Armed Forces Military Police Department

[2510] The departments will continue to be located at Sessvollmoen

[2511] The Armed Forces ABC School is organized under the Army today

[2512] The government will consolidate all professional education and skills development organized under a chief in each defense branch and operational unit

[2513] These changes are included in this consolidation

[2514] Increased civil-military cooperation on logistics

[2515] The government plans to base supply, maintenance and workshop services to a greater extent on the use of civilian suppliers where these have economies of scale and where this is not a core competency of the Armed Forces

[2516] A logistics concept has been developed for support to HV that has transfer value to other parts of the structure

[2517] For the future work, the new logistics concept for HV and the use of strategic agreements will be guidelines for the further development of other areas within the logistics business

[2518] This implies a potential for reducing logistics in the defense branches

[2519] This will primarily affect logistics bases, which could be reduced or closed as a result of the expansion of this type of agreement

[2520] Logistics Base Joint can be closed down and Logistics Base

[2521] Land is being reduced and closed down in line with the implementation of new logistics concepts where civilian suppliers carry out the tasks

[2522] A prerequisite for this is that civil agreements can cover the tasks cost-effectively and satisfactorily

[2523] There will also be potential for reduction of transport and storage capacity with new logistics concepts

[2524] An increasing number of new material systems are delivered with performance-based agreements for logistics throughout their life cycle, so-called Performance Based Logistics (PBL

[2525] This means that many of the premises for the system's performance and costs in the operational phase are included in the contract negotiations for the purchase of the equipment

[2526] Furthermore, third- and fourth-party actors are examples of solutions where another party assumes responsibility for managing logistics solutions for the Armed Forces

[2527] PBL and 4PL agreements are expected to become the dominant supply and maintenance solution of the future

[2528] Establishing such agreements will shift the interface between the Armed Forces and civilian suppliers

[2529] By entering into such contracts, the Armed Forces will be able to reduce staffing within material management, purchasing, warehousing and maintenance, because these are services that can be an integrated part of the performance that the Armed Forces agrees to purchase from suppliers

[2530] In addition, warehouse space can be reduced when tasks are moved to suppliers

[2531] It is a strategic goal to use the contract forms that provide the Armed Forces with the most cost-effective solutions

[2532] Modernization and reduction of the Armed Forces' stockpile

[2533] The Government has implemented a comprehensive modernization of the Norwegian Armed Forces' management and inventory structure based on modern principles for supply operations

[2534] During the period, FLO will centralize and consolidate the warehouse structure

[2535] The Armed Forces' inventory structure is planned to be halved

[2536] A key prerequisite for the Armed Forces to be able to establish a rational supply and material management structure is the transition from stationary stockpiles to material flow in combination with emergency stockpiles where necessary

[2537] This means that, especially for commercially available material, the Armed Forces' preparedness will be based to a greater extent than today on preparedness agreements rather than preparedness stocks, which has significant potential for gain

[2538] Where critically necessary, tactical storage of certain categories of material for departments with short readiness times will be carried out

[2541] The closure of Hovemoen will result in reduced expenses of approximately NOK 0.9 billion over a 20-year period, including reduced manyear costs

[2555] Overall consequences related to the restructuring of the base and support structure The measures to consolidate the base structure and modernize and streamline the support structure are one of the prerequisites for the financial balance of the entire defense structure

[2567] Allied exercises and training

[2568] It is a goal of the government to facilitate exercises and training for allies and partners in Norway

[2569] In this way, Norway contributes to allies strengthening their ability to operate under Norwegian climatic and geographical conditions, thereby increasing the credibility of collective defense guarantees in the event of crisis or armed conflict

[2570] A high level of regular allied presence creates a stabilizing normal state in peacetime, which contributes to credible deterrence and defense

[2571] The government continues the level of ambition for regular allied presence through exercises and training in Norway

[2572] It is also a goal that allied activities should be carried out to a greater extent integrated with national exercises and training, and that they be carried out at bases and in training areas where Norwegian units are stationed

[2573] This will provide a better connection with operational planning for allied operations in Norway and the allied activities carried out in peacetime

[2574] The government will continue the current concept where force producers establish cooperation agreements with relevant partners and conduct exercises and training within the framework of their own activities, while the Allied Training Center (ATS) has special responsibility for parts of the land-based training and exercise activities

[2575] Joint exercises between Norwegian and allied forces on Norwegian soil improve the ability to interact, and thus provide increased operational capability

[2576] ATS will continue in Northern Norway with headquarters in Porsanger

[2577] After the Åsegarden camp is decommissioned, the foreign exercises and training that are currently carried out there should be carried out to a greater extent together with Norwegian units at the bases where these units exercise and train

[2578] There may be a need to use civilian suppliers to establish temporary accommodation and catering, in order to have sufficient capacity during periods of particularly high activity

[2579] The Armed Forces have already entered into agreements with civilian actors, which provide the opportunity for the establishment of temporary bases with accommodation and catering, as well as other logistical support

[2580] There is potential for greater exploitation of such agreements

[2581] The government places emphasis on strengthening FOH's ability to plan and lead joint operational exercises

[2582] The government also wants to place increased emphasis on Norway regularly hosting allied exercises

[2584] The government recommends continuing the Host Country Support Battalion to support the US Marine Corps' advance depots in Trøndelag, and moving the Co-located Operating Base (COB) depot for combat aircraft from Bodø to Evenes and the COB depot for tanker aircraft from Sola to Rygge

[2586] The warehouses allow for the rapid receipt of American fighter jets and tanker aircraft

[2588] Without significant upgrades to the necessary infrastructure, it will be costly to restore the necessary capacity on Sola

[2589] A COB warehouse requires security, personnel and local support

[2591] It has a favorable location and an infrastructure that is well suited to this business, including the necessary fueling plant capacity and necessary parking spaces

[2592] Given that Allied fighter aircraft must be supported in the north, Evenes and Bardufoss are relevant bases after Bodø and Andøya have been closed

[2593] Banak is located too far east

[2595] Bardufoss is therefore not considered suitable

[2596] Evenes stands out as the most relevant air station for COB storage for combat aircraft

[2598] This provides synergy and facilitates cooperation, especially through regular allied presence in peacetime
