[2602] Societal impact assessments

[2603] Discontinuation of departments and closures of bases have consequences for employees, regions and local communities

[2604] The Ministry of Defence has therefore, in dialogue with the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation, carried out the necessary impact assessments

[2605] A district-level impact assessment (DKU) has been conducted to assess the ripple effects for local communities affected by the recommended measures

[2606] This includes quantifying how measures affect employment, settlement and service provision

[2607] An overall assessment is also given of how the measures impact on regional policy objectives

[2608] Of the identified measures, only Andøy will experience a significant drop in population and employment

[2609] The government has therefore chosen to conduct a socio-economic analysis, in line with the state system for calculations, in which alternative base solutions to the closure of Andoya air station are further impacted

[2610] Assessment of socio-economic profitability for the establishment of a forward combat aircraft and maritime surveillance base in the north

[2611] In the socio-economic analysis, a number of both priced and non-priced impacts of the five alternative base solutions have been considered

[2612] The alternative of concentrating the activity at Evenes is considered the best solution also from a societal perspective

[2613] The priced impacts in the socio-economic analysis are without VAT and other distributional impacts within the state, they are added to the state's financing costs (tax collection) and they are discounted by 4 percent per year

[2614] This means that the figures are not directly comparable with the other figures in the long-term plan, which reflect the actual costs for the defense sector

[2615] Table 6.1 shows the total priced impacts over 30 years

[2616] The comparison of the priced impacts shows the same picture as the Ministry of Defense's calculations, i.e. that the government's recommendation for a concentration of activity at Evenes is the most affordable alternative, both in terms of investments and operating costs

[2617] The zero option of continuing maritime patrol aircraft on Andøya and QRA without air defense and base defense at Evenes also entails significant costs for society, without providing the same defense capability as the other options

[2618] In the socio-economic analysis, the collaboration with Andøya Test Center (ATC), the release of land, noise pollution, environmental impacts and changes in local safety have been considered, among other things

[2619] The consequences for ATC have received particular attention

[2620] According to the socio-economic analysis, the base solutions affect ATC both positively and negatively

[2621] It would be positive that Norwegian air defense, which regularly purchases services from ATC, would be increased in scope and that an air defense department would be deployed in the immediate area

[2622] This applies to all base solutions

[2623] It will negatively affect ATC if Andøya is closed down, in that ATC's costs will increase, and they will thus have to increase the prices they charge for their services

[2624] This could negatively affect sales

[2625] These are services in high demand, nationally and internationally, and it is not considered likely that ATC's will have to close its operations due to the closure of Andøya air station

[2626] Where negative consequences for business and the municipal economy on one of the bases lead to positive consequences on the other base, the effect is considered a distributional impact in the socio-economic analysis

[2627] Relocating the Armed Forces' activities from Andøya to Evenes will result in relocation and lower activity on Andøya, which could have a major impact on the local community

[2628] Evenes, on the other hand, will experience correspondingly increased activity

[2629] Such distributional effects are described in the report, but will not affect socio-economic profitability

[2630] There are over 2,500 employees in Andøy municipality, and including the ripple effects of a closure of the air stations, according to DKU, a six to nine percent decrease in employment and an expected decrease in population of between six and ten percent are expected

[2631] This is significant, but when it is expected that about 90 percent of both employment and population will be maintained, Andøya will still be a sustainable local community

[2632] The closure of the air station may provide opportunities both through the release of land for the municipality and through opportunities for alternative value-creating activities in the facilities vacated by the Armed Forces

[2633] The Government assumes that the state's social responsibility for affected local communities and regions must be safeguarded when state reorganizations result in a significant reduction in activity levels

[2634] Closure of Andøya Air Station could result in a reduction in activity in a local community where the Armed Forces' activities have been important for many years

[2635] The local community of Haugnes was vacated to make room for the air station

[2636] The government is committed to ensuring that the municipality has good conditions for restructuring and further development after the closure of the airport

[2637] It will therefore be important to have a good dialogue with Andøy Municipality and Nordland County Municipality regarding the need for restructuring measures as a result of the changes in the Armed Forces' activities in the municipality

[2638] To succeed with such facilitation, the government emphasizes cooperation between the municipality, the county council, the business community and private initiators

[2652] Development of the defense sector's other agencies

[2653] The defense sector consists of the Ministry of Defense (MD) and five subordinate agencies

[2654] The Norwegian Armed Forces, Defence Materiel Administration (FMA), Defence Construction (FB), Defence Research Institute (FFI) and the National Security Authority (NSM

[2655] The operational capability of the armed forces and the defense of the country are the main mission of the defense sector

[2656] The primary function of the other four agencies will thus be to support the Ministry of Defense and the Armed Forces

[2657] The exception to this is the instruction authority that the Ministry of Justice and Public Security has over the NSM in matters within the Ministry of Justice and Public Security's area of responsibility

[2658] The support for the Armed Forces means that the development of the Armed Forces will affect the agencies' tasks

[2659] Defence Materiel and Defence Buildings in particular are consequence organisations and must therefore relate to how other elements in the Armed Forces are organised as a result of the long-term plan

[2660] All agencies must continuously work on improvement and efficiency so that the organization's quality and delivery ability are further strengthened

[2661] The agencies must continuously make adjustments to their own organization based on the needs and developments of the sector

[2662] All agencies shall seek to develop existing and new collaborative relationships nationally and internationally within the guidelines of the Ministry of Defence

[2663] In the work on this long-term plan, significant potential for efficiency improvements has been identified within the agencies' areas of responsibility

[2664] Defence Materiel will continue as an ordinary administrative body, directly subordinate to the Ministry of Defence

[2665] The agency was established on January 1, 2016, based on the transfer of parts of the activities of the Norwegian Armed Forces Logistics Organization

[2666] The purpose of establishing a separate materiel agency is to achieve stronger strategic management, including through shorter lines of management and responsibility

[2667] In addition, the purpose is to achieve quality improvement and efficiency of material investments and material management

[2668] The agency shall oversee materiel investments and materiel management in the defense sector and ensure that the Armed Forces and other agencies have access to cost-effective and secure materiel in line with adopted long-term plans

[2669] The main tasks of Defence Materiel shall be to plan, acquire, manage and dispose of materiel for the Armed Forces and other agencies in the defence sector

[2670] Defence Materiel shall be further developed as a professional practitioner within materiel investments and materiel management

[2671] Increased professionalization of investment activities means that the new agency will have the ability to scale and better utilize expertise across capacity areas, increased project expertise, and increased continuity in positions

[2672] Defence equipment must be developed with robust and sufficient expertise related to agency management

[2673] The agency shall consist of managers and employees with different expertise

[2674] Financial-administrative, technical, mercantile, legal and other relevant expertise within the agency's area of ​​responsibility is essential

[2675] Furthermore, it is essential that Defence Materiel has access to relevant military expertise

[2676] This will be done by assigning military personnel from the Armed Forces to Defence Materiel

[2677] Defence Materiel will continue to support the Armed Forces with technical expertise, to avoid duplication of expertise environments in the defence sector

[2678] Defence materiel is established through three phases, the first phase of which involved the establishment of an interim organization that prepared for the establishment of the agency

[2679] In the second phase, Defence Materiel will adapt the organization to become an efficient and functional agency

[2680] Defence Materiel will also make adjustments to the organization towards the desired organizational structure for effective task performance

[2681] In phase three (2017 and beyond), Defence Materiel will work on continued efficiency improvements so that the organization's quality and delivery capability are further improved

[2686] Specific goals will be given for efficiency improvements within these dimensions

[2687] Defence Buildings will continue as an ordinary administrative body, which, on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, exercises the ownership role for the defence sector's properties, buildings and structures (EBA

[2773] National Security Authority The National Security Authority (NSM) is a cross-sectoral directorate for preventive security services

[2774] subordinate to the Ministry of Defense

[2775] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has the right to instruct the NSM in matters within the ministry's area of responsibility

[2776] NSM shall primarily contribute to state security and societal safety

[2777] Only to the extent that the security of businesses and individuals is of importance to state security or societal security, shall this be included in NSM's activities

[2778] NSM's responsibilities and tasks are primarily regulated in the Preventive Security Service Act (Security Act) and regulations

[2779] The Security Act is under revision and the outcome of this could lead to changes to NSM's tasks

[2783] The agency will also provide information, advice and guidance to businesses and contribute to the development of security measures

[2784] NSM is the point of contact and has executive responsibility towards other countries and international organizations within the field of preventive security

[2785] NSM shall exercise certification authority for IT security in products and systems (CERTIT

[2829] Personnel and competence The right competence at the right time

[2830] Personnel are a crucial input factor for the Armed Forces

[2831] It is the personnel who transform the structures and weapons platforms into operational capability

[2832] The competence reform in the defense sector will contribute to the sector's development into a modern competence organization with the right competence at the right time, in the right place

[2833] It is crucial that the sector is able to attract, recruit, utilize, retain and develop the expertise it needs

[2834] It is equally important to retrain the skills that are no longer relevant

[2835] Three factors are of particular importance for the government's priorities in the area of personnel and expertise

[2836] Firstly, the priorities should help develop, improve and streamline the sector

[2837] This requires that businesses have the ability to be innovative

[2838] Secondly, the new arrangement for military personnel entails extensive changes to the personnel structure, which means that recruitment activities, selection and education must be adapted to new career paths

[2839] The scheme is better adapted to the need for specialization, in-depth expertise and continuity, and is crucial for balancing the age and rank structure in the Armed Forces

[2840] Thirdly, the priorities must be seen in the context of the government's commitment to increasing the staffing of the operational part of the structure by moving resources from management and base operations to operational activity

[2841] The consequence of this is that the Armed Forces must change its personnel composition and reallocate resources as part of the continuous modernization of the Armed Forces

[2842] The skills reform was introduced in

[2843] A defense for our time, and further concretized in Meld

[2844] St. 14 (2012–2013) Competence for a new era

[2845] The goals of broader recruitment, increased diversity and flexibility, improved competence flow between the defense sector and the rest of society, and development of in-depth competence and specialization will be continued in the coming four-year period

[2846] New and more relevant expertise will also be added

[2847] The Government will facilitate better utilization of the sector's professional military expertise and prioritize this for operational activities

[2848] The best possible use of permanent personnel and reservists in the Armed Forces must also be ensured

[2849] Recruitment and selection

[2850] The military profession is becoming increasingly differentiated and specialized, and modern defense is completely dependent on heavy technical and professional expertise

[2851] The specialist corps will form the backbone of the future Armed Forces

[2852] These will represent continuity and experience-based professional expertise

[2853] The role of officers is changing as the specialist corps grows and takes shape

[2854] The Armed Forces need officers with perspectives on their own activities, who inspire, motivate and mobilize for effort and the solution of demanding tasks

[2855] The Armed Forces will need fewer officers in the future

[2856] The officers are still dependent on having a certain degree of specialized professional competence, but in the future they will represent a greater degree of broad military expertise and leadership

[2857] The education of officers must also change as a result of new roles

[2858] Officers and specialists should complement each other, work complementarily and not duplicate roles and tasks

[2859] This requires differentiated selection

[2860] The term competence is used to refer to formal qualifications, but also encompasses experience, personal qualities, skills and attitudes required to complete a task

[2861] A significant part of the defense sector's competence needs is covered through education at the Armed Forces' various schools

[2862] In addition, there is a need for expertise in a number of other fields

[2863] The Norwegian Armed Forces' personnel policy lays the foundation for how the Armed Forces will recruit, retain and further develop both military and civilian employees with high motivation and the right expertise

[2864] The needs and dimensioning tasks of the Armed Forces shall be the guiding principle

[2865] A greater degree of competence flow between the defense sector and civilian society is a personnel policy objective, and the sector must see its competence needs and its competence production as part of society's overall resources

[2866] A challenge in the coming four-year period will be to create a personnel and competence structure that supports the operational structure

[2867] Staff and support functions will be reduced, and resources will be prioritized for operational activities

[2868] At the same time as the Armed Forces need to reallocate personnel and downsize, there will also be a need to strengthen staffing within certain areas of expertise

[2869] This is necessary to help shift a larger part of the personnel composition towards operational structure and relevant support structure

[2870] Conscription and initial service General conscription is fixed and must be developed continuously to be best adapted to the needs of the Armed Forces

[2871] The first-time service will be further developed and adapted to the Armed Forces' requirements for responsiveness, operational departments' need for flexibility and freedom of action, as well as increased requirements for competence and cost-effectiveness

[2872] Conscription contributes to the Armed Forces' tasks and constitutes an important part of the Armed Forces' operational capability

[2873] This is particularly true for tasks related to emergency preparedness and national defense, which require force building based on access to conscripted personnel

[2874] The introduction of general conscription for women and men from 2015 was an important step forward in the modernization of conscription

[2876] Conscription allows the Armed Forces to select those most suitable for initial service

[2885] The initial service will primarily be used to contribute to the Armed Forces' standing units

[2887] Consideration of the need to obtain good operational benefits from basic soldier training, while also allowing the competence to be reused in the reserves or the Home Guard, must be emphasized when the length of initial service is assessed

[2889] This will ensure that the time between completion of initial service and transfer to the Home Guard is reduced

[2890] The selection scheme will be developed to ensure that the Armed Forces recruit the most suitable among the most motivated for initial service to an even greater extent

[2913] The Armed Forces' education system The Armed Forces are a competence organization, and cover a significant part of the diverse competence needs through their own education system

[2914] The Government will reform the Armed Forces' education system in a way that preserves the characteristics of military professional education and ensures good quality in education

[2915] To ensure the right expertise at the right time, the Armed Forces depend on relevant and good military education delivered in a cost-effective manner

[2916] A review of the education system was announced in the competence report (Report

[2917] St. 14 (2012–

[2918] The Government will create better conditions for quality in education, facilitate more robust academic environments, strengthen research-based education and at the same time free up resources

[2919] Several of the recommended measures have also been discussed in previous long-term plans

[2920] The Government has emphasized that the Armed Forces' education system be harmonized with the structural reform in the university and college sector (Report

[2921] St. 18 (2014–2015)) as far as appropriate

[2922] By concentrating resources in fewer but stronger institutions, the ambition is to create more robust academic environments and better research

[2923] At the same time, it is an objective to maintain the sector's uniqueness and regional structure

[2924] Need for change

[2925] Today's education system appears fragmented, costly, with complex governance lines and often small and vulnerable academic environments

[2926] The education system must be adapted to the military system, which establishes two complementary career systems with a career path for officers (OF) and a career path for commanders, grenadiers and constables (OR/specialists

[2927] This changes the focus of the education system to vocational and functional education

[2928] A future distribution between officers and specialists of 30 percent and 70 percent, respectively, affects the need for advanced professional education for both categories

[2929] Changes related to the military system, and the government's proposals for efficiency improvements for the coming period, will result in changed educational volumes with a reduction in the need for officer training and a decrease in the number of students at the three military academies

[2930] To successfully implement the military system, it is essential that not only new education is developed for specialists, but that measures are also implemented to ensure the relevance and attractiveness of future officer education

[2931] The proposals for change are therefore mainly aimed at level-building education

[2932] The start of an educational reform

[2933] The main tasks of the Armed Forces' education system are to conduct education, research and development, training and dissemination within military core competencies

[2934] The education system should deliver relevant, needs-tested, flexible, cost-effective and good military education

[2935] The purpose is to provide the Armed Forces and the defense sector with professional military expertise

[2936] Military personnel must be able to solve tasks and exercise leadership in very demanding situations

[2937] The Government will reform the Armed Forces' education system in a way that preserves the unique nature of military professional education and ensures good quality in education

[2938] At the same time, the Armed Forces must have institutions for higher education that are well anchored in civil society and that follow civilian development trends where appropriate

[2939] The following shall be the basis for the development of educational activities

[2940] – Create an education system

[2941] All education and competence production should be seen in context with the aim of creating better conditions for quality in education and reducing costs

[2942] Governance and management must be clarified

[2943] This is a prerequisite for improving the education system both qualitatively and cost-wise

[2944] – Prioritize core military competencies

[2945] The Norwegian Armed Forces' education system shall develop the knowledge, attitudes and skills necessary to plan, conduct and lead military operations

[2946] Necessary civilian competence is generally trained in civilian settings, recruited after completion of training and given military training

[2947] – More joint education

[2948] Education should be made common where possible, in order to develop common core military competence, strengthen quality and reduce costs

[2949] – More needs-based and flexible education

[2950] The starting point should be the individual's competence needs in relation to the requirements of the position

[2951] The purpose is to avoid costs for training personnel who either do not need the training or already have equivalent training

[2952] The education should be timely and sufficient, and as a general rule be modular, so that it can meet different needs for military development or education

[2953] More modular education creates increased flexibility for joint education across the defense branches and enables better utilization of civilian educational institutions

[2954] More civil cooperation

[2955] Increased collaboration with civilian educational and research institutions will increase the quality of research, development and education, and help reduce costs

[2956] Civilian educational offerings should not be duplicated

[2957] – More collection of features

[2958] As a general rule, there should be as few providers of the same type of education as possible

[2959] Joint solutions should be sought to the greatest extent possible where appropriate to keep quality good and costs down

[2960] – More robust professional environments

[2961] The Armed Forces must have robust academic environments to ensure quality in education

[2962] This will be ensured, among other things, through better internal collaboration, both between the level-forming education, between the various weapons schools, and across level-forming education and vocational and functional education

[2963] The institutions should not duplicate, but utilize each other's and civilian educational and expertise environments

[2964] The education system should compare itself with other civilian and military education systems nationally and internationally in order to establish a basis for comparison in terms of quality and cost

[2965] – More harmonization with the civil sector

[2966] A good balance should be created between organized learning activities and time for independent study so that students are equipped to take responsibility for their own learning

[2967] Compensation and incentives for academic staff and students should be harmonized to a greater extent with the civilian university and college sector

[2968] The individual employee should be given greater responsibility for completing the necessary education for further career advancement

[2969] Box 8.1 Today's education system

[2970] Basic military education is the general and basic military education at command schools, war schools and colleges

[2971] Specialized subject- and function-oriented education takes place mainly at the Armed Forces' weapons schools and competence centers

[2972] The Norwegian Armed Forces' education system costs a total of approximately NOK 2.5 billion per year, of which NOK 1.1 billion goes to level-building education and NOK 1.4 billion to vocational and functional education

[2973] The educational institutions are spread across 16 geographical locations, and consist of six schools that provide basic officer education, five accredited colleges that provide over ten bachelor's degrees, one accredited college that provides master's degrees, and ten vocational schools that provide vocational and functional education

[2974] In 2015, the education system included 20 master's degree students, 66 staff study students, 619 bachelor's students, of which 495 were military academy students (annual cohort totaling approximately 190 students), and 901 officer trainees on shorter and longer officer courses

[2975] In addition, a large number completed vocational and functional education at the various vocational schools

[2976] Necessary organizational changes

[2977] The Government will implement three measures that contribute to clearer governance and management of the Armed Forces' education system

[2978] These measures are prerequisites for contributing to future high-quality military education and for reducing educational costs

[2979] Establish overall responsibility for the education system

[2980] The first measure is to establish strategic management of the entire education system, both the level-forming education and the more branched, subject- and function-oriented education at the weapons schools

[2981] This management function is added to the Defence Staff, which assumes the Chief of Defence's overall responsibility for education

[2982] The responsibility involves management and control of the education system based on the framework set by the Ministry of Defense

[2983] From six colleges to one joint college

[2984] The second measure involves a change in the current management and organizational model within level-forming education

[2985] The government will establish a joint university college in the Armed Forces by organizationally merging the current six accredited universities (the Norwegian War College, the Norwegian Naval Academy, the Norwegian Air Force Academy, the Norwegian Defence College of Engineering, the Norwegian Defence Intelligence College and the Norwegian Defence College

[2986] The current location will be continued and the individual schools will retain their names and will continue to have their own school principals

[2987] The new joint college will be responsible for all level-forming education for both officers and specialists, as well as other accredited professional education

[2988] The command schools are also being brought together organizationally under the new college to exploit synergies between command and officer education, and ensure better utilization of teaching staff across the educational levels

[2989] The college will be responsible for delivering level-building education based on guidelines, assignments and resources provided by the Defence Staff

[2990] A board of directors will be established for the new college, which will be the school's highest academic body and replace a number of coordinating councils for advanced education currently led by the Norwegian Armed Forces College

[2991] Management lines and budget funds are moved from the defense branches and other operating units in the Armed Forces to the reorganized college

[2992] It is a prerequisite that the heads of the defense branches and other central operating units are ensured real professional influence on level-forming education and accredited vocational education through representation on the board of the new college

[2993] The principles in the main model for state universities and university colleges shall be applied

[2994] When merging the colleges, academic and administrative resources belonging to the six colleges will be considered in context to ensure more cost-effective operations and create better conditions for quality education when organizing the new college

[2995] The new joint university college will follow the Universities and University Colleges Act as required by accreditation

[2996] Future management and leadership of vocational and functional education The third measure is to create conditions for future management and leadership of vocational and functional education, which will become the main focus of the education system after the implementation of the military system

[2997] The government will therefore organizationally merge the weapons schools into one school environment in each defense branch/operational unit with a head responsible for the defense branch/operational unit's competence production

[2998] Quality-enhancing and cost-reducing measures

[2999] How studies are structured, the proportion of joint subjects, the degree of civil cooperation and the degree of emphasis on independent studies in the educational courses, have a lot to say about the quality and costs of the education

[3047] The armed forces' force structure is not fully established in daily operations

[3048] Departments and units in the Army, Navy and Air Force, as well as joint departments, are to varying degrees dependent on fully trained and trained conscript reserve personnel in the event of force build-up to solve especially the most demanding of the Armed Forces' missions

[3049] Also, high-priority units such as the Telemark Battalion and the special forces, the Air Force and the Navy bases are, to varying degrees, dependent on such a reserve addition in order to reach full operational capability

[3050] In part, the reserve will fill positions that are not staffed on a daily basis, and in part, the reserve must be able to replace conscripts in their first time service where they have not yet reached a level of education where they can be used to complete all assignments

[3051] Allied countries that are natural to compare ourselves with, in addition to countries like Sweden and Finland, have a two-part force structure consisting of a standing force component and a reserve component

[3052] This applies both to countries with conscripted military forces and to countries that use conscription

[3053] A reserve component ensures operational capability for the most extensive but least likely challenges

[3054] The reserve also contributes to increased endurance, for example in long-term international efforts, without incurring large operating costs when the reserves' operational capabilities are not required

[3055] Conscription reserve

[3056] The need for heightened preparedness places demands on the Armed Forces' ability to rapidly and simultaneously build up forces

[3057] what was previously the Chief of Defence's pool of conscripts will be replaced by identified and trained conscript reserves in all branches of defence

[3058] The purpose of the reserve is to ensure that all units in the Armed Forces can be manned in a predictable manner with sufficiently trained and practiced personnel within the specified readiness times

[3059] The reserve will be trained and exercised regularly in line with the Armed Forces' needs, and will be recruited from the personnel and expertise acquired through initial service

[3060] The reserve will primarily be based on military service, but motivation and volunteerism will also be emphasized when recruiting personnel after completing initial service

[3061] In line with the Armed Forces' needs, a limited proportion of the reserve will also be voluntary, similar to the concept for the Home Guard's task forces

[3062] Such a voluntary reserve will be able to fill positions where special requirements are made, for example regarding training and practice levels

[3063] A voluntary reserve could also contribute to increased endurance, including in international efforts, readiness for NATO or the EU's standing forces

[3064] The Home Guard's regional structure will also be staffed with personnel on active duty in the future

[3065] When the Chief of Defence's force pool is closed, the allocation to the Home Guard will take place directly after the completion of initial service, without intermediate allocation to the force pool

[3066] This will give the Home Guard access to personnel with more up-to-date military expertise

[3067] Operational useful life in

[3068] Home security will also be able to be improved, if necessary

[3069] The Home Guard's task forces will still be based on volunteers

[3070] Reservists with civilian specialist expertise

[3071] The Armed Forces' need for expertise is diverse, and specialist expertise can be both difficult to access and expensive to acquire

[3072] Among the personnel who complete initial service, officer training school or war school, there are many who, after completing their service, take civilian education or otherwise acquire civilian competence that the Armed Forces may need

[3073] The Armed Forces should be able to draw on the civilian expertise and willingness of personnel to use this in the Armed Forces to a greater extent than is currently the case

[3074] Management of reservist personnel The Armed Forces' new personnel management system will enable the Armed Forces to better maintain an overview of the competence of available personnel

[3075] Reservists with relevant expertise should be used to a greater extent to meet time-limited needs in the Armed Forces, where the need goes beyond what the Armed Forces can impose through conscription according to current laws and regulations

[3076] This type of service must therefore be based on volunteerism

[3077] The use of reservists should not cover permanent skills needs

[3078] The Armed Forces have a time-limited need for specialist expertise in certain positions

[3079] This expertise is covered by either permanent employees or hired personnel, which in many cases is very expensive

[3080] A temporary need may arise, for example, in connection with exercises, health examinations of a large number of people upon entry, certification and inspection of equipment, or tasks related to international operations

[3081] By opening up a more active use of reservists based on their civilian expertise, reservists can fill positions and functions where the Armed Forces have temporary and time-limited expertise needs

[3082] The need for this type of reservist is estimated at about 100 people, but the scheme will have potential for expansion

[3083] The Armed Forces should facilitate the provision of necessary military training to civilian volunteers with special expertise, so that they can enter into temporary and time-limited contracts with the Armed Forces to perform specific functions

[3084] A risk and cost assessment must be the basis for determining which groups such a scheme should cover, and the relationship with the main employer must be clarified before such agreements are entered into

[3085] Reservists in the Armed Forces can in future constitute a personnel reinforcement of the Armed Forces' departments and units in peacetime, as well as in emergency situations and operations

[3086] Such a concept has the potential to both cut costly contracts and free up man-years where the need for expertise can be met by reservists

[3087] The use of reservists must be based on a thorough assessment of the competency requirements for the individual position and the needs of the Armed Forces

[3088] The government will return with a proposal for a legal basis for reservists

[3089] There is a need for a restructuring of the Armed Forces' personnel structure to free up positions and resources to strengthen operational activities, and to recruit new and relevant expertise

[3106] The goal is to strengthen interaction with the civil sector, especially at the municipal level

[3107] The government's policy includes personnel from the foreign, justice and defense sectors who have participated or are participating in peacekeeping, peacemaking or state-building efforts in other countries

[3157] The defence sector's R&D should complement civil R&D, and be the basis for multinational cooperation and contributions to industrial and technological development and innovation

[3158] R&D can make an important contribution before, during and after investments in equipment and property, buildings and structures

R&D must be based on the challenges and threats facing Norway, and research must be at the forefront of developments in the new threat landscape

Information and communication technology (ICT) Further investment will be made in ICT in the defence sector to enable the Armed Forces to carry out their most important tasks, and to contribute to good utilisation of the sector's resources

[3217] The use of ICT is a prerequisite for establishing situational awareness, leading military forces and using modern weapons

[3218] ICT shall be used as a means for improved collaboration in the Armed Forces' operations and to streamline force production and management in the defense sector

[3219] Technological developments mean that ICT equipment is becoming smaller, less expensive, more user-friendly and has higher performance

[3220] The development allows for the storage, processing, analysis and sharing of ever-increasing amounts of data in near real time

[3221] At the same time, ICT services become more flexible and robust by making them less dependent on the physical infrastructure

[3222] At the same time, complexity means increased costs, and civilian use is driving developments in ICT to a greater extent than before

[3223] Other countries and actors will therefore have access to, and use much of, the same technology that Norway has

[3224] Military-adapted and applied ICT is referred to as the Armed Forces Information Infrastructure (INI

[3225] Modern crisis management and warfare are characterized by short timelines, complex situations, and a high need for information

[3226] To improve the Armed Forces' ability to conduct high-intensity combat and manage crises, the ability to make and implement timely decisions must be strengthened

[3227] Better situational understanding can be achieved by increasingly collating data from many sources and making it available to users at different levels

[3228] Sensors, weapons and platforms are linked together, regardless of the branch of defense and type of weapon, to contribute to increased operational capability

[3229] The ability to support consistent information exchange from combat technical to strategic levels is strengthened through standardization of core services and flexible solutions for securing and exchanging information

[3230] It should be dimensioned for an increased information volume

[3231] Automated decision support tools for compiling and analyzing information from multiple sources should be utilized to a greater extent

[3232] To establish access to INI in areas in need of improved capacity, especially in the high north, a combination of stationary, deployable and mobile systems will be used

[3233] It will also be relevant to increase the use of elevated platforms such as manned and unmanned aerial platforms and satellites

[3234] Allied operations in Norway and Norwegian participation in NATO operations abroad depend on INI being able to interact with the alliance's ICT systems

[3235] An increased focus on ICT that supports coordination and operational interaction with NATO will therefore be emphasized, including more robust communication channels

[3236] Such an improvement in the ability to interact both within one's own organization and also with NATO will have a major impact on operational capability

[3237] Coordination within total defense and cross-sectoral crisis management requires that relevant actors can communicate through compatible communication channels

[3238] The defense sector will therefore also consider such interaction needs when the sector's ICT is further developed

[3239] In the long term, better interoperable ICT systems can reduce the number of systems necessary to support total defense

[3240] To protect information and to be able to utilize ICT effectively in peace, crisis and armed conflict, it must be protected against attack, exploitation by an adversary and breaches due to unintended events

[3241] INI must therefore be resilient

[3242] This means that it must have an inherent ability to adapt the flow of information to changing conditions, both during and after extraordinary stresses, even when events occur unexpectedly

[3243] Such adaptability includes redundancy and the ability to regenerate ICT infrastructure in the event of unwanted events

[3244] To further strengthen ICT security, national encryption systems will be further developed

[3245] During this four-year period, special emphasis will be placed on the development of ICT that supports the defense sector's interaction with NATO and partners

[3246] Furthermore, the use of common ICT systems in the sector will be increased to ensure better interaction and utilization of the combined resources

[3247] ICT will be developed with greater capacity and better coverage, especially for mobile devices

[3248] Data center solutions and operational and monitoring tools for INI will be established for enhanced resilience and ICT security

[3249] The Government will further develop cooperation between the Armed Forces and the police within the ICT area to support interaction within the total defense and contribute to the effective utilization of the overall ICT resources

[3250] The focus on ICT means that overall costs related to ICT will increase in the next four-year period

[3251] Harmonization of the ICT portfolio in the defense sector, standardization and increased use of ICT developed for civilian purposes also for military purposes, shall contribute to the financing of the investment in ICT. **9.3 Preventive security** The framework conditions for Norwegian security have changed since the previous long-term plan for the defense sector was prepared

[3252] This has also led to an increased likelihood of the defense sector being exposed to espionage, sabotage, and terrorist acts

[3253] Such events can be difficult to predict, and they can have serious consequences for our security or that of our allies

[3254] Norway is also affected by other developments, such as digitalization and globalization

[3255] Overall, this places great demands on preventive security in the defense sector, and requires a systematic and long-term approach to the work of improving the security situation in the sector

[3256] Objectives for preventive security The purpose of preventive security in the defense sector is to counter threats to the sector's values and protect them against espionage, sabotage and terrorist acts

[3257] This is done through preventive security measures, detection and handling of security-threatening incidents

[3258] The preventive security service in the defense sector shall support the security and defense policy priorities and contribute to increasing the operational capability of the Armed Forces

[3259] Digitalization and technological development create a number of opportunities for the defense sector, but at the same time increase vulnerability to digital threats

[3260] It is crucial to ensure that the information is correct, that it is available, and that unauthorized persons do not have access to it

[3261] In addition, it is essential to have traceability in the event of a violation of one of these three principles

[3262] It is essential that objects that are to be protected against espionage, terrorism and sabotage are identified and protected in accordance with applicable regulations

[3263] Objects worthy of protection must be continuously identified and secured in accordance with the requirements laid down in the Security Act and regulations

[3264] Agencies in the defense sector must have good routines for authorizing personnel, and the clearance and authorization work must maintain a high professional level

[3265] The clearance authorities in the sector shall prioritize satisfactory processing times for clearance cases

[3266] Safety culture is the sum of employees' knowledge, motivation, attitudes and behavior

[3267] A good safety culture, together with technological and organizational security measures, is a prerequisite for effective risk prevention and handling of safety-threatening incidents

[3268] In the defense sector, the safety culture must be good

[3269] I CT is of fundamental importance for the defense sector to be able to carry out its tasks in military operations and in daily activities

[3270] At the same time, digital attacks are a significant and growing threat to Norwegian authorities and businesses

[3271] For the defense sector, the threat in peacetime is particularly related to foreign intelligence activities

[3272] Foreign states, groups and individuals may seek knowledge about conditions in Norway that can be used politically, economically or militarily

[3273] Technological developments make the defense sector vulnerable to digital espionage and reinforce the need for protection of sensitive information

[3274] Digital attacks have become an integral part of military operations

[3275] Such operations could also be directed against Norway

[3276] The defense sector must be prepared to be exposed to digital attacks in times of crisis and armed conflict

[3277] Vulnerabilities in ICT infrastructure can have negative consequences for the sector's ability to perform its tasks, especially at the upper end of the crisis spectrum

[3278] Good cooperation between ICT response environments and the various operational organizations in the defense sector is a prerequisite for preventing, detecting and handling ICT attacks

[3279] There is no single common ICT response environment for the defense sector

[3280] There is potential to increase the ability to handle serious ICT attacks in the defense sector by establishing such an environment

[3281] The establishment of a common ICT response environment for the defense sector, which will function as the sector's point of contact with the cross-sectoral, national ICT response environment in NSM, will therefore be investigated

[3282] As part of the investigation, it will also be assessed what role such a possible sector response environment should have with regard to military information sharing with NATO

[3283] Different and fragmented ICT solutions for unclassified communication between the Armed Forces and external actors can be a security risk

[3284] From a security perspective, the number of ungraded networks and ICT platforms should therefore be reduced and subject to better control

[3285] At the same time, the Armed Forces' need to be able to collaborate effectively with partners must be met

[3286] It is important for the defense sector that the ability to communicate both internally within the agencies and between the agencies and the ministry is maintained, both in daily operations and throughout the entire crisis spectrum

[3287] Secure Public Network (SPN) is infrastructure that can be disconnected from the internet when needed, but still maintain the ability for data communication between users of the network

[3288] Such a disconnection may be relevant, among other things, if critical national values are affected by major ICT attacks

[3289] During the four-year period, it will be assessed whether and, if so, how the defense sector should contribute to the further development of SON

[3290] At the upper end of the crisis spectrum, the ability to communicate with NATO is particularly important

[3291] Ensuring such communication should therefore be emphasized in preventive security work

[3292] As described in Chapter 4 on total defence, the defence sector is dependent on civilian infrastructure and service production to carry out its tasks

[3293] This dependence will be reinforced in a serious crisis situation and in armed conflict

[3294] The Armed Forces are therefore mapping their need for support from civil society

[3295] It is also necessary to consider whether the defense sector as a whole has additional dependencies on civilian infrastructure and civilian services

[3354] During the period, the Ministry of Defence will consider alternatives for the future management of the national fortifications, so that the preservation of cultural and historical properties is carried out without conflicting with the sector's primary tasks. **10 Choices and priorities in implementation 2017–2020** **10.1 Implementation capacity** This long-term plan facilitates a relevant and sustainable defence where availability and endurance, readiness and renewal of equipment will be strengthened to increase the Armed Forces' operational capability in both the short and long term

[3355] This chapter summarizes the main lines of the long-term plan and operationalizes the government's security and defense policy, including the choices and priorities that are made for the period

[3356] The chapter further describes the government's goals for the activities in the defense sector with associated assumptions and financial frameworks, as well as key success criteria

[3357] The Community makes significant resources available to the defence sector

[3358] The government sets high standards for managing resources efficiently and in line with current laws, regulations and political decisions

[3359] The defense sector must be characterized by good and efficient financial management, sound administration, and the ability and willingness to constantly innovate and improve, thereby facilitating increased operational capability

[3360] This places high demands on competence and leadership involvement at all levels, including good attitudes anchored in clear ethical guidelines

[3361] Within the framework of the Security Act, there must be transparency regarding resource use and results

[3362] The breadth of operational capabilities in the Armed Forces is being reduced somewhat in order to strengthen availability and preparedness, as well as continue and, towards the end of the period 2017–2020, step up the modernization of a number of materiel systems

[3363] The operational capability will be strengthened, among other things, through more efficient force production in the Armed Forces, by Defence Construction delivering buildings based on standardized solutions at an agreed time and price, and by Defence Materiel acquiring more fully developed equipment and delivering services at an agreed quality, time and price

[3364] Close coordination and interaction between these agencies, and good governance, are crucial to ensuring the necessary implementation capacity during the four-year period

[3365] The National Security Authority (NSM) and the Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI) have important deliveries to the defence sector, and increased emphasis should be placed on their support of the operational capability of the Defence Forces

[3366] In addition, NSM and FFI must carry out their assigned civil duties

[3367] Through the entirety of the measures and goals set out in this proposition, a solid foundation is established for the long-term development of the defense sector, so that the Armed Forces remain a relevant security policy instrument for Norway

[3368] For the government, the central goal is that the defense sector can fulfill its missions within a comprehensive and responsible framework in the short and long term

[3369] The government emphasizes giving the agencies in the defense sector the necessary freedom of action in the assignment process

[3370] With increased freedom of action comes increased responsibility for achieving clearly defined operational, financial and administrative results, within the framework of political decisions

[3371] By ensuring that management, based on risk and materiality, is based to a greater extent on the timely implementation of reforms and structural and ambition changes, the Ministry of Defence will facilitate increased implementation capacity in the defence sector

[3372] The will and ability to set comprehensive long-term priorities are crucial in this context

[3373] The extensive cost calculations that form the basis for the decisions put forward in this proposal are based on a number of assumptions, including a significant increase in the budget framework for the defense sector in the period

[3374] Any deviations from the planned increase in defense budgets will have consequences for implementation and must be handled structurally and in a multi-year perspective, and accompanied by any necessary adjustments in the level of ambition

[3375] A unified defense sector** The main purpose of Norwegian security and defense policy is to ensure Norway's sovereignty, territorial integrity and political freedom of action

[3376] The Armed Forces, with support from the sector's combined resources and within the framework of NATO's collective defense, are the central security policy instrument that will ensure Norway's sovereignty, Norwegian rights and preserve Norwegian freedom of action against military and other pressure

[3377] The government's proposal for a long-term plan for the defense sector ensures that each agency in the sector will contribute to solving its missions within a defined and sustainable level of ambition

[3378] The Armed Forces must be able to carry out its nine tasks within the specified level of ambition

[3379] The deliveries from the other agencies in the defense sector are crucial input factors in enabling the Defense Forces to solve these tasks effectively and in a good manner

[3380] In parallel with the sector continuously fulfilling its tasks, the entirety of the measures that follow from this proposition must be realized

[3381] Overall, it is these two considerations that set the framework for the formulation of the objectives for the defense sector, and thus for the management in the period

[3382] The whole must be balanced in a responsible, efficient and sustainable way

[3383] In the Ministry of Defence's management, the strategic goals are specified in a comprehensive target picture for the defence sector, from which given goals for the individual agency are derived with associated periodized milestones and management parameters

[3384] This periodization of the goals, together with the annual goal and performance requirements, provides a management basis for the Ministry of Defence's follow-up of progress in this long-term plan

[3643] The Chief of Defence's comments on the government's recommendation on the further development of the Armed Forces Introduction In the professional military council of 1 October 2015, I presented my principled view on the development of the Armed Forces

[3644] I will subsequently provide a professional military assessment of the government's recommendations

[3645] The changing security policy situation in Europe and in areas that affect European security, as well as the financial situation in the Armed Forces, were the starting point for the formation of the professional military council

[3646] In my advice to the government, I emphasized the Armed Forces' need for a financial boost in order to be a credible and relevant first-line defense for NATO in Norway

[3647] It is very positive that the government, through this proposal, is planning a significant economic boost and promoting a long-term balanced plan

[3648] Where I, in the professional military council, organized the Armed Forces with a balance of capabilities in all domains to solve the most difficult tasks on Norwegian territory, the government has considered several perspectives and to a greater extent based on an organization that prioritizes maritime conditions in the north

[3649] The proposal is nevertheless largely consistent with the recommendation of the professional military council

[3650] The government prioritizes strategic capacities in the sea and air domains and, in the short term, downplays the modernization of capacities in the land domain

[3651] The plan is to create a defense that will be modern, maintain good quality and have the ability to solve a wide range of tasks

[3652] I support the government's priority of making the structure we already have work as intended, and then aligning the Armed Forces with future military and security policy challenges and threats. **The operational structure of the Armed Forces** In the professional military council, I emphasized shaping a defense that is capable of meeting the most serious military challenges to Norway

[3653] This is a defense that is conceptually built around basic capabilities

[3654] The Armed Forces must have the ability to provide as early warning as possible and be able to establish and maintain situational awareness at strategic, operational and tactical levels

[3655] The ability to identify and understand threats forms the basis for taking relevant measures

[3656] The armed forces must have the ability to lead and conduct operations through a good command and control apparatus

[3657] This entails clear management lines, secure and efficient communication solutions and adapted infrastructure

[3658] The defense must have the necessary firepower both to deter an opponent and to hit him in a counterattack

[3659] This requires that the Armed Forces operate in close cooperation between the Army, the Home Guard, the Navy, the Air Force, the Armed Forces' Special Forces and the support functions

[3660] The armed forces must have the ability to protect their weapons systems, bases and units

[3661] Particularly important in this context is credible air control, consisting of both fighter aircraft and air defense

[3662] The structure must have preparedness and mobility with an adapted supply and logistics capacity that provides the necessary responsiveness, availability, endurance and presence in priority areas

[3663] The government has continued these basic capabilities in the proposed defense structure, and the structure is largely consistent with my recommendation in the professional military council

[3664] The proposal's recommended structure is a good basis for the Armed Forces to be able to carry out the assigned tasks

[3665] The Government prioritizes removing the mismatch between the Armed Forces' operational capability and the needs resulting from the changed security policy situation

[3666] However, this will take longer than desirable from a professional military standpoint

[3667] Preparedness and capability for action are improved through strengthened staffing and increased allocations for training, maintenance, spare parts and emergency supplies, and through an increased presence of modern naval and air forces in Northern Norway

[3668] The Armed Forces' capabilities within intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance are being renewed and strengthened with the government's proposal

[3669] The acquisition of new maritime patrol aircraft to replace the P-3 Orion continues maritime surveillance capacity and anti-submarine warfare capabilities

[3670] The proposal, to a lesser extent than what I recommended, calls for the Armed Forces to exploit the opportunities that open up through the use of unmanned vehicles

[3671] The technological development in this area is large and forward-looking, and the technology is well suited for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance

[3672] The Air Force will be provided with the necessary capabilities to conduct effective air control, air surveillance, combat targets and support other parts of the Armed Forces

[3673] The acquisition of 52 F-35s provides the Norwegian Armed Forces and NATO with a strategic capability that contributes to credible deterrence, and it will ensure sufficient control of our own airspace so that our own or NATO's ground and naval forces can operate

[3674] The ability to protect important bases, divisions, allied reinforcements and critical infrastructure is strengthened by acquiring more and better air defense systems

[3675] The Navy's endurance and presence are improved through more crews and an increased number of sailing days

[3676] Submarines are an important strategic capability, and a new acquisition will provide credible deterrence and strengthen the Norwegian Armed Forces' combat power

[3677] The introduction of autonomous systems against naval mines enables the Navy to carry out its tasks in a new and cost-effective way

[3678] The Norwegian Armed Forces' special forces are further developing their capabilities to conduct special forces operations, including counter-terrorism tasks

[3679] The collection of Bell helicopters at Rygge as a dedicated resource for the special forces will contribute to this

[3680] The Bell helicopters have limited capacity and a replacement of the helicopters is not a priority in the proposal

[3681] If the mobility of special forces is to be maintained over time, a replacement must be considered over the 20-year period

[3682] The government's recommended development of the land force is essentially a continuation of the current organization and equipment

[3683] This is a solution that does not correspond to the conceptual framework that I put forward in my professional military council

[3684] Renewal of the Army's firepower and protection is being postponed and the gathering of firepower in the north is not being prioritized

[3685] The government proposes a separate land power study to look at the development of land power

[3686] It is important that this is implemented as soon as possible and that the government clarifies the direction and ambition for the land force before the work is initiated

[3687] The establishment of a hunting company in Finnmark should await clarification of the future land power

[3688] The government's recommendations regarding closures and reductions in structure, in order to strengthen other parts of the operational structure, are consistent with my recommendation

[3689] The Armed Forces' support activities build upon the operational capability

[3690] The Armed Forces must have their own capacity for support in the operational area

[3691] In addition to this, I agree that civilian and commercial actors should be used to a greater extent where it is appropriate in terms of preparedness and resource-efficient

[3692] Bases and establishments

[3693] It is crucial for the long-term balance of the Armed Forces that the base and support structure is adapted to the operational structure

[3694] I would also like to emphasize the importance of gathering the Armed Forces' activities around the country's central transportation arteries

[3695] This is important for the most efficient reception and further movement of allied reinforcements, and will lead to better utilization of logistics capacities, ICT and other important infrastructure

[3696] I support the government's emphasis on these principles, and that costly bases with little or no operational value are not maintained

[3697] The Norwegian Armed Forces' education system develops knowledge, attitudes and skills necessary to plan, conduct and lead military operations

[3698] In my professional military council, I emphasized that today's education is of high quality

[3699] However, the cost is high and efforts must be made to reduce it

[3700] This will require the education system to be simplified

[3701] My recommendation was to wait with structural changes until the Armed Forces have implemented a new military system and experiences with it have been mapped

[3702] However, the government is recommending a comprehensive overhaul of the education system without any experience with the new military system and apparently without having thoroughly assessed the consequences of the solution

[3703] I am concerned that a lack of impact assessments may contribute to an overly optimistic savings potential in education

[3704] The government's recommendation to significantly strengthen the defense budget over the next 20 years marks a historic boost for the Armed Forces

[3705] Realizing this financial promise will be crucial for developing a future relevant defense

[3706] It is positive that the government is now taking into account the real cost growth associated with the acquisition and operation of defense equipment in its economic planning

[3707] In addition to increased appropriations, the government's focus is based on freeing up significant resources through efficiency improvements and structural changes

[3708] Experience after years of restructuring and streamlining in the Armed Forces is that both the potential for gains and the pace of implementation are often estimated too optimistically

[3709] In my professional military council, I proposed a significant streamlining, but the proposition goes further in assessing the potential for gains

[3710] My concern is whether the assessment is too optimistic, and that it will be very demanding to realize the full savings potential

[3711] If this cannot be realized, it will weaken the operational strengthening that the proposition describes

[3712] Multinational cooperation could contribute to more efficient resource utilization, both in terms of capability development and operational activities

[3713] Multinational cooperation is demanding, however, and results will depend on the willingness and ability of countries to adapt national requirements

[3714] Conclusion** Through this proposition, the government has made a choice in the long-term development of the Armed Forces, which I consider to be very positive

[3715] A historic economic boost over the 20-year period lays the foundation for developing a relevant defense that is capable of solving the assigned tasks

[3716] The realization of the relevant Defence will require both the responsible authorities to finance the plan and the Defence to realize the ambitious savings potential

[3717] The government largely proposes to change the Armed Forces in line with my professional military advice

[3718] The Armed Forces are being developed with sufficient operational capability to meet security policy challenges

[3719] Furthermore, the government prioritizes increasing the preparedness and relevance of the capacities we already have, before modernizing and renewing the structure
